title: ESPN return dates (US) compared with Moscow-dated games: the night game before the return day counts as available
claim: injuryFactor compares the Sports.ru game's Moscow date with ESPN's returnDate, which is a US Eastern date. A US evening game on returnDate-1 is filed under Moscow date returnDate, so the code counts it at 1 (or ends the GTD 0.5) one game early. US matinees on the return day are filed under the same date and are handled correctly, so the rule must depend on tip-off.
evidence: Cross-check: ESPN 2026-10-20T23:00Z PHI@NY is filed by Sports.ru under 2026-10-21; BOS@DET at 19:00Z is under 2026-10-20 (same US date). tz.mjs over the live report finds 0 players currently affected (most returnDates are 10-21/22 and first games are US-dated on or after them). In season the error recurs with probability about 0.45 per return (chance of a club game on the US day before).
impact: Up to +1 expected game (× share × per-game) per returning player, about 5-20 FP on week/month horizons.
fix: Convert each game to its US date (ESPN start time, or Moscow date - 1 for games before 08:00 MSK) before comparing with returnDate.

title: Season horizon misses the 2 NBA Cup games per club (calendar has 80 of 82); every season number will jump in December
claim: Sports.ru club calendars currently list 80 games for each of the 30 clubs. The 2 Cup-determined regular-season games are added only in December, so rest-of-season expected points are about 2.4% low for everyone until then. Rankings barely change, but absolute season forecasts (standings 'Прогноз сезона', team KPIs) are biased, and chainCurve is calibrated on 82 while 80 are applied.
evidence: live-sports-current.json: Counter({80: 30}) games per club; last date 2027-04-12. A healthy 82-game player gets 77.6 code season games (80 × .97).
impact: Season totals about 2 games × share × per-game low (about 30-60 FP for starters) until the calendar is updated.
fix: Add 82 - len(calendar) placeholder games spread over December (or scale the season horizon by 82/len) until Sports.ru publishes them; state it in the UI.

title: Telegram confidence wording can print '70%' with 'умеренно' (rounding vs. level)
claim: sureness() prints Math.round(conf*100) next to why.level, which is computed from the unrounded value. The UI deliberately floors to avoid exactly this, so conf = .695-.699 prints 'Уверенность 70%: умеренно' and the message says 'не уверенно'.
evidence: Math.round(0.6996*100) = 70 while 0.6996 < CONFIDENT (.7) gives level MODERATE; the UI comment at season-ui.js:130 documents the same issue.
impact: Contradictory Telegram text on borderline moves.
fix: Use Math.floor as in the UI, or derive the level from the printed percent.

title: Deployed DB copy predates the bonus removal: per-game priors still contain ±1 FP/g team result while game points exclude it
claim: The audited default-draft.json (generatedAt 2026-10-20T12:18Z) was built before commit 73328bf (12:29Z). forecast.meanPerGame still includes components.teamResult. perGame() blends that prior with Sports.ru points minus the result bonus, so in-season estimates mix two formulas until the Pages build is redone.
evidence: python on public/data/default-draft.json: teamResult component mean -0.002, min -0.946 (Alex Karaban), max +1.027 (Thomas Sorber); 244 players with |teamResult| > 0.5 FP/g.
impact: Strong-club players about +0.5-1 FP/g and weak-club players about -0.5-1 FP/g in priors (about 10-13 FP per month horizon) until rebuilt. It decays as games arrive.
fix: Confirm that the Pages workflow rebuilt the DB from f5c0328. Add a build assertion that components.teamResult is absent when league-rules.json says the bonus is removed.

title: Objective is expected FP only; the league prize is rank (P(1st) in an 8-team total-points race)
claim: bestPackage/recommendation maximize expected points subject to a season floor. With standings decided by final total FP, a team's P(finish 1st) ≈ P(T_me > max T_others), and that depends on variance. A trailing team gains from variance-seeking moves, a leader from variance-reducing ones. The per-player spreads needed to evaluate this already exist (pointsSpread), and teammate correlations are about 0 (clubCorrelation -0.002).
evidence: Theory: with totals approximately normal, P(win) = E[prod_j Phi((mu_me - mu_j)/sqrt(s_me^2 + s_j^2))] (independent rivals approximation). A move with dMu = -10 and dSigma = +80 raises P(win) for a team 300 FP behind with sigma about 600. Not backtested here.
impact: Late-season decisions for teams far behind or far ahead.
fix: Offer an optional 'шанс на 1-е место' objective. Monte-Carlo the 8 team totals with per-player spreads and rank candidate packages by delta P(1st) (or expected final rank). Validate on 2025-26 replays.

title: A transfer-day game is credited to the buyer, though nearly every game on that Moscow date ended before transfers open at 08:00 MSK
claim: stints() opens the new player's stint with from=x.date and closes the old one with to=x.date. teamPoints/teamFact/playerFact then count a game for the buyer when g.date>=from and for the seller only when g.date<to. Sports.ru dates games by Moscow date. A Moscow date D carries the overnight games (US date D-1 evening, tip-off 00:00-07:00 MSK). These are already over or in progress when the FBL transfer window opens (08:00-22:00 MSK). On Yahoo ('Daily - Today', the league's scoring) and on Sports.ru (players lock at tip-off), such a game belongs to whoever held the player at tip-off, which is the seller. The app does the opposite. The team that makes the move is credited with the incoming player's game from the previous night and loses the outgoing player's. The code contradicts itself: transferWeek() (season.js:31) assumes 'a move on a week's last day (after its games)', while stints() treats a move on D as if it happened before D's games. The same mis-assignment applies to the live 'В игре' column, because running points are summed over the current roster. Only Moscow-evening games (US afternoon games, about 5-8% of the season) are handled correctly by the date rule. Grey zone: the real result also depends on when the league mirrors the move on Yahoo, which the app never sees.
evidence: Synthetic repro (node, scratch t2.mjs): team 0 sells Sabonis and buys Ejiofor on 2026-10-27, transfer seen at 10:00 MSK. Both played overnight on Moscow date 27.10: Sabonis 40, Ejiofor 10. Ejiofor also scored 20 on 28.10. App teamPoints[0] = 30 and teamFact(week) = 30; the correct value is 60 (40 + 20). Stints printed: Sabonis {from:'2026-10-20', to:'2026-10-27'}, Ejiofor {from:'2026-10-27'}. ESPN tip-off times confirm the calendar uses Moscow dates and that most games are overnight: 20.10 BOS@DET 22:00 MSK is dated '2026-10-20'; PHI@NY 02:00 and OKC@SA 04:30 MSK are dated '2026-10-21'; 15 of the 16 games in the first 3 days tip off between 00:00 and 08:00 MSK. Magnitude, from 2025-26 logs (top-160 players, FBL formula, Monte Carlo of 200k random swaps): P(error≠0) = 0.595, mean |error| = 8.75 FP per transfer, sd 13.5. Selling an injured player: buyer over-credited +6.33 FP per transfer on average. Buying the morning after a top-20% game (classic streaming): the app credits that very game, 27.2 FP of phantom points per transfer (median 26). With 3 transfers a week this can reach about 80 FP per week.
impact: Every team's official total, period facts, per-player facts and live column are wrong on every transfer day where the incoming or outgoing player had an overnight game, which is about 60% of transfers. The error is biased in favour of active streamers, can be exploited, and moves close standings (forecast gaps between neighbouring teams are 19-800 FP).
fix: Attribute by tip-off time. Store each calendar game's tip-off time (ESPN scoreboard event.date, matched by Moscow date and the two clubs) and keep the transfer's time bounds (seenAfter, seenAt] in the stint. A game counts for the seller if tip < seenAfter and for the buyer if tip >= seenAt. If the tip falls inside the window, show it as disputed. If times are missing, use a date-only fallback: seller gets g.date<=s.to and buyer gets g.date>s.from, except games on date D with tip >= 08:00 MSK, which go to the buyer. Apply the same rule to playerFact and to the running 'now' column. Regression test: transfer on D with both players playing overnight on D; the team keeps O's game on D and not I's.

title: A player held by two FBL teams is counted in full for both (team totals, period facts, place and season forecast)
location: src/season.js:44-46, src/season.js:52-57, src/season.js:247-254, src/season-ui.js:137, src/season-ui.js:251-256, src/rules.js:105-127
claim: seasonRosters deliberately lets a second FBL team buy a player another FBL team holds (Sports.ru allows it). stints are keyed by team and player, so teamPoints and teamFact credit every game of that player to both teams, and standingsTable adds his remaining-season expectation to both forecasts. The league rule (one FBL team per player, the later buyer is in breach) and Yahoo, the scoring platform, cannot put one player on two teams of one league. In the real standings only the first holder can score him. The rules tab already identifies the first holder (firstHolder/'before'), but the totals ignore it.
evidence: Synthetic repro (scratch t3.mjs): team 1 buys Sabonis, already on team 0, on 2026-10-27. Sabonis then scores 50 in a single game. Output: teamPoints [50, 50], league sum 100 for one 50-point game. leaguePlace: team 0 rank 1 'вровень', team 1 rank 2. checkRules flags team 1: 'Domantas Sabonis уже в составе «The Balkan Murderers» — игрок может быть только в одной команде лиги'. Live data today has no shared players (scratch t1.mjs 'shared []').
impact: Rare but large when it happens: about 25-45 FP per game of the shared player, inflating the later buyer for as long as the breach stands. It also moves that team's place and season forecast.
fix: In teamPoints/teamFact/playerFact, credit overlapping stints of one player only to the holder that firstHolder() rules 'before'. Credit neither and show a ⚠ in the table when the order is 'same' (undetermined). Exclude the shared player's expectation from the later buyer's 'Прогноз'. Add a test that the league-wide sum of credited points equals the sum of points of distinct (player, game) pairs.

title: FBL game points rely on a calendar-orientation vote and silently fall back to Sports.ru points (with the result bonus), although each player's own game row already holds all the stats and a home-first score
claim: fbl_points subtracts a result bonus inferred from the club-calendar score, using the orientation voted by score_orientation. A game keeps Sports.ru's own points, bonus included, without any flag in three cases: orientation is None (no game with both calendars scored, or a club calendar never collected); the calendar has no score yet; or the (date, opponent, home) lookup misses. The result is a file that mixes FBL and Sports.ru scoring. The front end never reads live.gamePoints or live.errors, so it cannot tell. The current live file (collected 12:34Z, before f5c0328) has no gamePoints field at all. The detour is unnecessary: parse_games throws away columns the Sports.ru game table has on every row (2О, В20, 3О, В3О, Ш, ВШ, ПБ, ПР, Ф, ПХ, П, БШ, О, МИН and 'Счет'). From these the FBL formula can be computed exactly, and the row's score is home-first, which gives a built-in integrity check (ФО − FBL must equal the bonus of that result). ACCEPTANCE.md:228 and league-rules gamePoints state that played-game points are FBL's; this holds only when every lookup succeeds.
evidence: Fetched two Sports.ru pages for 2025/26 (Jokic 1887865, bench player 2116570) and parsed them with the collector's own regexes (scratch py/table.py). Over 113 played games, ФО − FBL(row stats, +2 if MIN≥10 else +1) ∈ {+2,+3,−2,−3}, and it matches the home-first row score in 113/113 games (home win +2: 33, away win +3: 22, home loss −3: 25, away loss −2: 33), including 34 games under 10 minutes. Synthetic runs of fbl_points: (a) game 1 has a calendar score, game 2 not yet → [('2026-11-01', 28, 'W', 30), ('2026-11-02', 33, None, None)]: the second keeps the bonus, unflagged. (b) Only one club's calendar collected → (None, 0) and every game keeps Sports.ru points. (c) A game listed 'В гостях' in both calendars → both teams recorded 'L'. grep: no reference to gamePoints, sportsPoints or live.errors anywhere in src/.
impact: When a fallback fires, the affected games carry ±2-3 FP of bonus, and this flows into team totals, form and the in-season per-game update (rateGames 20/30). Systematically, players of winning clubs are overstated and those of losing clubs understated, which is exactly the effect the league removed on 20.10.
fix: In parse_games, keep the stat columns and the row's 'Счет'. Compute points = О+ПБ+ПР+ПХ+БШ−(В20+В3О−2О−3О)−(ВШ−Ш)−2·П−Ф+(2 if МИН≥10 else 1) and keep ФО as sportsPoints. Assert that ФО − points equals result_bonus(home, row score home-first), and count any mismatch into gamePoints.mismatches. Keep the calendar path only as a cross-check. In the UI, warn when gamePoints is missing or reports unconverted games or mismatches.

title: The league's Yahoo categories have no minutes, so the '+2 if ≥10 min else +1' part of the FBL formula cannot come from Yahoo; the docs claim 'the same categories as Sports.ru's formula'
claim: Yahoo keeps rotisserie category totals: GP, FGA, FGM, FTA, FTM, PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK, TO, PF. There is no MIN category. From season totals the league can only add c·GP, with c = 1 or 2. It cannot apply Sports.ru's per-game rule of 2 points at 10+ minutes and 1 below, which the app uses for facts (via Sports.ru ФО), for the ESPN live points and for every forecast. ACCEPTANCE.md:227 says Yahoo has 'the same categories as Sports.ru's formula', which is false: the formula also needs minutes. Which constant the league actually uses is undecided and unrecorded.
evidence: league-rules.json statCategories = [GP, FGA, FGM, FTA, FTM, PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK, TO, PF]. Sports.ru rows confirm the minute rule is part of Sports.ru ФO: 34 games under 10 minutes give +1 (scratch py output). 2025-26 logs, top-160 players: games under 10 minutes = 130 of 11068 = 1.17%. App season expected games per team: 648-718 (scratch t1.mjs).
impact: If the league uses +2·GP, the app undercounts by about 8 FP per team per season (negligible). If it uses +1·GP, every number in the app is about 1 FP per game too high: roughly 650-720 FP per team (about 5%), per-game forecasts 1 point high, and relative standings shifted by the difference in games played (up to about 70 FP between teams).
fix: Ask the league owner which per-game constant the Yahoo totals get. Record it in league-rules.json (e.g. scoringFormula.gameBonus: 'GP*2' or 'minutes rule'). Make boxScorePoints and the collector use it, and fix ACCEPTANCE.md:227. If the minute rule stays, document that the league must take minutes from box scores outside Yahoo.

title: Stale or false method text after f5c0328: points labelled 'официальные ФО Sports.ru', and 'вес прогноза — 10 матчей' (actually 20/30 games of minutes)
location: src/season-ui.js:413, src/season-ui.js:415, src/season-ui.js:639, src/season-ui.js:640, src/season-ui.js:642, src/season.js:74, src/season.js:84-89
claim: Since f5c0328 the points the app shows are FBL points (Sports.ru's minus the team result bonus), plus live ESPN points in the place. The Teams-tab and Overview text still say otherwise: the place tooltip 'по официальным ФО Sports.ru'; the period tooltip 'Факт — официальные очки Sports.ru за период'; METHOD.overview 'Очки — официальные фэнтези-очки Sports.ru'; METHOD.teams 'Место в лиге — … по официальным очкам' (the place also includes uncounted live games). A user comparing with Sports.ru's own team points will see a difference of ±2-3 per game that the text says should not exist. METHOD.transfers, which is also shown on the Teams tab, says the per-game forecast moves toward actual points with 'вес прогноза — 10 матчей' and 'по формуле Sports.ru'. PRIOR_GAMES=10 is used only when minutes are missing. Every database forecast has minutes, so the real weights are rateGames 20 (established) or 30 (newcomers) games of minutes, and minuteGames 5/2 with half-lives of 20/5 games. In the place KPI the fact includes live games, while the 'ФО · период' fact next to it excludes them.
evidence: forecast.minutes>0 for 874 of 874 players (scratch t5.mjs), so perGame always takes the calibrated path (season.js:84). data/inseason-calibration.json: established {rateGames:20, minuteGames:5, minuteHalfLife:20}, newcomer {rateGames:30, minuteGames:2, minuteHalfLife:5}. Texts quoted from the listed lines.
impact: Every user of the Teams tab and Overview is told something false about what the numbers are and how the forecast reacts to games (it reacts 2-3 times more slowly than stated). Mismatches with Sports.ru will look like bugs.
fix: Rename to 'очки FBL (формула Sports.ru без бонуса за результат)'. State that the place includes uncounted live games. Replace '10 матчей' with the calibrated weights read from CALIBRATION (e.g. 'вес прогноза — 20 матчей игрового времени, у новичков 30'), and generate the text from the JSON so it cannot drift again.

title: 'Прогноз сезона' in the standings is a no-transfer, 80-game projection: about 2.4% low for everyone and biased against teams with fragile players, so it ranks differently from the draft tab's season score
claim: rest = Σ expectedPoints over the current 10 players for the club-calendar games left. (1) Each club calendar currently lists 80 games. The 2 NBA Cup knockout or make-up games per club are not scheduled yet, so every season forecast misses about 2/82 of the season until December. (2) Missed games count as 0 for the rest of the season, as if no team ever replaced an absent or injured player, although the league allows 3 transfers a week. The draft tab's season model adds exactly that replacement value (forecast.transfer.value, slotSeason). The two tabs therefore project different orders for the same rosters, and the Overview 'Прогноз' understates teams built on injury-prone stars.
evidence: Scratch t6.mjs on the live rosters: app season forecast / Σ meanSeason = 0.976-0.981 for all 8 teams (80/82 = 0.9756). Expected games 648-718 versus forecast games 664-733 (−14 to −17 per team). Every club has 80 calendar games, and calendars are symmetric. Replacement value per team: 630-1115 FP. Ranking by the app forecast: 0, 3, 2, 1, 6, 7, 5, 4. Ranking by Σ slotSeason: 0, 3, 2, 6, 1, 4, 5, 7. Team 4 (Haliburton, Wagner, Zubac, Gobert: transfer value 1115) is last at 12307 in the app but 6th at 13113 by slotSeason; team 7 is 6th in the app but last by slotSeason.
impact: The season forecast shown on the Overview, in the Teams KPI and in per-player 'Факт / прогноз' (season horizon) is about 300-350 FP per team too low. Middle and bottom ranks change depending on which tab the user looks at.
fix: Until Sports.ru publishes the Cup games, scale each club's remaining expectation by 82/len(calendar), or add placeholder games in week 8. Add replacement value for the absences the chain expects: (club games − expected games) × the replacement level per game affordable with the bank, as forecast.transfer does. Otherwise label the column 'Прогноз без трансферов' and show both numbers.

title: No probability for the final place: standings and place are point estimates, though the top two forecasts are a coin flip
claim: leaguePlace sorts official plus live totals. standingsTable shows deterministic forecast totals. Nowhere does the season tab express uncertainty about the final place, while the draft tab has a full place simulation (simulation.js seasonSensitivitySimulations). With calibrated season ranges already in each forecast (seasonFloor/Ceiling, forward-conformal), a Monte Carlo or normal approximation of fact plus remaining-season points gives P(place) for every team. The remaining-season spread should shrink both with the fraction of the season left and with games played (rel·sqrt(k/(k+n)), as pointsSpread already does for swaps).
evidence: Scratch t4.mjs, 20k draws, split-normal per player from the forecast's 10/90 range rescaled to the app's expectation, players independent (clubCorrelation ≈ 0). Team sd 1243-1363 FP against forecast gaps of 165 FP (#1 vs #2) and 19 FP (#5 vs #6). P(1st): team 0 0.36, team 3 0.33, team 2 0.12, team 1 0.08, teams 6/7/5/4 0.04/0.03/0.03/0.02. Row and column sums of the place matrix = 1.00.
impact: Users read 'Прогноз сезона' as a predicted order, when #1 against #2 is about 36% against 33%. The probability of a place is the decision-relevant quantity for risk-taking moves late in the season.
fix: Reuse seasonSensitivitySimulations' engine with current rosters: fact so far plus rest-of-season draws (spread ∝ remaining expectation, shrunk by sqrt(k/(k+n)), plus per-game noise of sd game·sqrt(G); club shocks via clubCorrelation). Show P(1st) and P(top-3) in the place KPI and an 80% interval in the table. Measure with the Brier score of P(1st) on 2023-24..2025-26 replayed leagues; it should beat the deterministic rank (Brier of 0/1 picks).

title: Ties are broken differently on the Overview (by forecast) and in the Teams-tab place (by team index), and a tie for 1st shows '−0 до 1-го'
claim: standingsTable sorts by official+now, then by forecast total. leaguePlace sorts by total, then by team index. METHOD.teams claims the place is 'как в таблице на «Обзоре»'. Ties are routine on the first days of the season, when every team without a player in the games played so far has 0, so the two screens show different places for the same team. A team level with the leader but placed 2nd shows '−0 до 1-го' instead of a shared place.
evidence: Scratch t9.mjs, night 1 (only BOS@DET played, 20 points per BOS/DET player): Overview order 7 2 1 5 0 3 6 4, while the Teams-tab places are team 1: 2, team 2: 3, team 6: 8, team 4: 7. Teams 1/2 and 4/6 are swapped between the screens.
impact: Contradictory places on the first days (from tomorrow) and whenever totals tie. Cosmetic otherwise.
fix: Use one comparator for both screens. Better, show shared places for equal totals ('2–4'), and print 'вровень с 1-м' instead of '−0'.

title: '4 недели' means four Sports.ru tours on the Teams tab but 28 days in the replacement gains shown in the same rows
claim: windows().month runs to the end of the third tour after the current one. horizons().month, used by transferOptions in the replacement panel opened from the same row and by all transfer gains, is today+27. Both are labelled '4 недели' / 'за 4 недели'.
evidence: Scratch t8.mjs. On 2026-10-26 the Teams window runs to 11-16 and the gains to 11-22. On 2026-11-30: 12-21 against 12-27, i.e. 22 days against 28 (−21%). On 2026-12-05: 01-04 against 01-01.
impact: The roster row's forecast and the swap gains next to it cover windows that differ by up to 6 days. Low, but confusing.
fix: Pick one definition, preferably the tours, which match Sports.ru's weekly limits, and show the window dates next to the gain cells.

title: Week windows by Moscow date put Sports.ru week-14 games (US MLK-day matinees on Moscow 18.01) into week 13
claim: gameWeeks/week_ranges cut weeks by date. Sports.ru numbers weeks by US day: 3 games on Moscow 2027-01-18 (DET@CLE 20:00, PHI@ATL 22:30, BOS@WSH 23:00 MSK, all US Monday 18.01) are week 14 in the calendar. The app's week-13 window (12.01-18.01) counts them, so the 'Неделя' fact and forecast for tours 13 and 14 are off by those games.
evidence: Scratch t8.mjs: 6 club-calendar entries whose Sports.ru week (14) differs from the app window (13): Бостон, Вашингтон, Филадельфия, Детройт, Атланта, Кливленд on 2027-01-18. ESPN tip-off times for 20270118 confirm all three are Moscow-evening (US afternoon) games.
impact: Only the week-13/14 fact and forecast for the players involved: about 3 games of 30 clubs' worth.
fix: Assign games to tours by the calendar's own g.week (club calendar entry of that date) instead of by date range, in teamFact/playerFact and in expectedPoints windows.

title: Zero availability hazards make the absence chain give 100% play probability, ignoring the player's own season share
claim: chainCurve scales the hazards so that the 82-game mean equals the share. With hazards [0,0], every multiplier gives mean 1 ≥ share, so the curve is all ones. The player is then expected to play every remaining game rather than his season share (comment at 147-150: 'without hazards … it is the flat season share').
evidence: 5 database players have hazards [0,0]: Knueppel, Podziemski, Bridges, Champagnie, Carrington. Scratch t11.mjs: Knueppel (team 0, forecast 78 games, share 0.951) gets 80.0 expected games of the 80 left instead of 76.1, which is +69 FP. Podziemski (team 3, 79 games) gets 80.0 instead of 77.1, which is +45 FP.
impact: Inflates the season and 4-week expectation of these players by 3-5% (45-70 FP per season). This affects the two top-forecast teams and the transfer gains involving these players.
fix: In chainCurve, fall back to the flat share when h[0]+h[1] <= 0 or when the bisection cannot bring the mean down to share. Test: hazards [0,0] with share 0.95 should give expected games 0.95·n.

title: playRate after a mid-season trade counts the new club's games played before the player arrived as missed
claim: team = max(own rows, finished games of the current club's calendar, games on). After a trade, the new club's finished count includes games played before the player joined. If that club has played more games than his own team games, the extra games become missed games and lower his play rate, and with it all his expected points.
evidence: Scratch t10.mjs: 41 team games with the old club (played 40), new club with 43 finished games: playRate 0.937, against 0.968 using his own 41 team games (−3.2%).
impact: Traded players' rest-of-season expectations are understated by a few percent, since clubs differ by up to 3-4 games at the trade deadline.
fix: Count team games from the player's own Sports.ru rows (DNP rows included), and use the club calendar only from the date of his first row with that club.

title: A same-day transfer gives the bought player the games played that morning and takes them from the sold player
claim: stints() starts the bought player's stint and ends the sold player's stint on the journal date D. teamPoints/teamFact/playerFact then count g.date>=from && g.date<to. Sports.ru files each game under the Moscow date of tip-off, and FBL transfers are legal only from 08:00 to 22:00 MSK. So nearly every game dated D is a US-evening game that tipped between 00:00 and 07:59 MSK, hours before any legal transfer on D. The code credits that game to the incoming player, who was not on the team yet, and drops it for the outgoing player, who was. Under Yahoo's daily lineups the old player keeps that game and the new player cannot have it.
evidence: Date convention checked against ESPN: BOS@DET 2026-10-20T19:00Z is filed by Sports.ru as 2026-10-20, PHI@NY 2026-10-20T23:00Z as 2026-10-21, ATL@ORL 2026-10-21T23:00Z as 2026-10-22. Reproduction (scratch stint.mjs): transfer P1->P81 on 2026-10-25. P1 played 30 on 10-23 and 40 on 10-25; P81 played 35 on 10-25 and 20 on 10-27. teamPoints gives 85; the correct total is 90 (30+40+20). Magnitude from the 2025-26 logs, top-160 players, random transfer days (stint_mag.py): P(a player played on a given game day)=0.42. Mean |error| is 9.3 FP per transfer (sd 13.9). Selling a player who is not playing (an injured sale) adds a systematic +6.7 FP per transfer. With 50 transfers per team-season the random error alone has sd ~98 FP per team. The existing test (season.test.js:111) uses a 10-22 transfer with games on 10-21 and 10-23, so it never covers the same-day case.
impact: The league table ('Место в лиге', overview standings), the team 'Факт' per week/4 weeks/season and each player's 'Факт' are all wrong for every team that transfers. The error has a positive bias for teams that sell injured players. In a close 8-team race it can flip places.
fix: Treat the transfer moment as the boundary, not the date. The sold player keeps games with date<=D that tipped before the transfer; the bought player gets games that tipped after it. Without tip times the near-exact proxy is: old stint covers g.date<=s.to, new stint covers g.date>s.from, plus same-day games that tip after seenAt (store the tip time from the ESPN scoreboard, or note that Moscow dates for games before 08:00 MSK belong to the previous US day). Apply the same rule in teamFact and playerFact. Add a test where both players play on the transfer's Moscow date.

title: Points of played games depend on calendar scores even though each game row already carries the full box score
claim: fbl_points subtracts the result bonus by looking up the score in the club calendars and inferring its orientation. When the calendar has no score (calendar drops past games, majority-vote calendar from a page cached before the result, a failed calendar parse), it silently keeps Sports.ru's number with the ±2/3 bonus. gamePoints.gamesWithResult is written but nothing compares it with the number of played games or shows it. The player's own game table already holds every column the FBL formula needs and the score (home first). parse_games throws those columns away.
evidence: One GET of Jokic's 2025/26 page (?s=1317725). The table header is Дата, Соперник, Д/Г, Счет, МИН, 2О, В20, 3О, В3О, Ш, ВШ, ПБ, ПР, Ф, ПХ, П, БШ, О, ФО, С. Computing FBL from these columns plus the +2 home win / +3 away win / −3 home loss / −2 away loss bonus gives 65/65 played rows exactly equal to ФО when the score is read home-first (33/65 own-first). fbl_points itself works when calendars have scores: 65/65 exact for both orientations (fbl_points_check.py). Today all 2400 calendar rows have score=None, so whether past scores stay in the calendar cannot be verified yet.
impact: If the fallback triggers, every affected game is off by +2/+3 (win) or −2/−3 (loss). That is about ±1 FP/game for strong or weak clubs, flowing into perGame, form, team totals and transfer advice, with no warning anywhere.
fix: Parse the box-score columns in parse_games: fgm=2О+3О, fga=В20+В3О, ftm=Ш, fta=ВШ, pts=О, reb=ПБ, ast=ПР, stl=ПХ, blk=БШ, tov=П, pf=Ф, minutes. Set points to the FBL formula directly and keep ФО as sportsPoints. Assert FBL+bonus==ФО per row using the row's own score as a self-check, and alert when the check fails. This also yields the Yahoo category totals (GP, FGA, FGM, FTA, FTM, PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK, TO, PF), so the league's Yahoo standings can be replicated exactly. At minimum, raise an error when gamesWithResult < played games.

title: The quality guard does not see a broken game table or calendar, so official points or all forecasts can vanish silently
claim: quality() only measures the share of players with a price and a position. If Sports.ru renames the 'ФО' or 'МИН' header, parse_games returns [] for every player. If the calendar markup changes ('неделя'), parse_calendar returns [] and clubs={}. The snapshot is still published. merge_full only restores players missing from the collection, not emptied game lists. Downstream: teamPoints goes to 0 (standings say 'очков пока нет'), perGame reverts to priors, and expectedPoints has no calendar games, so every forecast and every swap gain is 0 ('Сейчас лучше не тратить трансферы', no Telegram alerts). fbl_points sees no scores and keeps the bonus.
evidence: guard.py on the real Jokic page: games parsed 82 as published, 0 with the header renamed ФО->ФО*. Calendar rows 80 as published, 0 with 'неделя'->'тур'. quality() on a pool with every game list and calendar empty returns (1.0, 1.0), above the 0.9/0.9 thresholds, so it is published.
impact: After a single layout change, every number on the season tab and in the Telegram feed would be wrong or zero until someone notices, with no 'stale/failed' message.
fix: Extend quality(): require calendars for at least 28 of 30 clubs, each with ~80+ rows. In season, require that the share of players with a non-empty game list does not drop by more than X% against the previous snapshot. On failure keep the previous clubs/games (as done for prices) and add an error the UI shows.

title: Merging the 2-hour collection overwrites the watcher's newer balance, roster and transfer count
claim: merge_full takes each team entry from the full collection, whose profile, balance, transfersLeft and roster were read at the collection's start T0. Only the journal and journalReadAt come from the watcher's snapshot. A deal the watcher applied during the 4-8 minute collection (fresh profile and roster read by apply()) keeps its journal row, but its balance, transfersLeft and roster go back to the pre-deal T0 values. They stay that way until the team's next journal change or the next full collection, 2 hours later.
evidence: merge_race.py. full (T0) has balance 200, transfersLeft 3, roster [Сабонис]. cur (T0+2min, after the deal Сабонис->Уайт) has balance 500, transfersLeft 2, roster [Уайт]. merge_full gives balance 200, transfersLeft 3, roster ['Сабонис'], journal deals [('Сабонис','Уайт')].
impact: For roughly 3-7% of deals (collection time / 120 min), for up to 2 h: (1) the transfer assistant and Telegram advice use a stale bank (here 300 too low), which can rule out affordable buys or propose unaffordable ones; (2) allTransfers flags 'Состав по журналу расходится с составом Sports.ru', and later league-feed protocols for that team turn into 'На проверке'; (3) Sports.ru's transfersLeft is stale.
fix: In merge_full, per team, keep the profile fields (balance, value, transfersLeft, transfersUnlimited, place, roster) from whichever source read them later. Store a profileReadAt in apply() and in collect_teams and compare the two.

title: A failed ESPN injury fetch leaves the snapshot without injuries, and the Telegram advisor then treats every player as healthy
claim: espn_injuries() returns None on any error, and the new snapshot then has no espnInjuries key. merge_full does not carry over the previous one. notify-transfers builds ctx.injuries from live.espnInjuries only. parseInjuries(undefined) is an empty Map, so injuryFactor=1 for everybody.
evidence: Code path: main() sets out['espnInjuries'] only if out_injuries. merge_full copies teams' journals and missing players, nothing else. notify-transfers.mjs:28 is injuries:parseInjuries(live.espnInjuries). season.js:256-258 iterates feed?.injuries||[], giving an empty Map. The browser UI falls back to fetching ESPN directly; the Telegram notifier does not.
impact: For up to 2 h after an ESPN outage, marketAlerts, bestPackage, transferVerdict and injuredTargets in Telegram rank OUT players as fully available. That can produce a 'buy' alert for an injured player or miss an injured roster player in the 'hurt' list.
fix: In merge_full, keep cur['espnInjuries'] when full lacks it, and mark it with its fetchedAt. In the notifier, refuse injury-sensitive alerts, or say 'травмы не обновлены', when espnInjuries is missing or older than N hours.

title: UI method notes and tooltips describe the points and update weights incorrectly after #84/#86; a documented audit count does not match the data
claim: (1) The overview, team KPIs and method notes call the points 'официальные (фэнтези-)очки Sports.ru'. Since f5c0328 they are Sports.ru's points minus the team result bonus, i.e. FBL's, not Sports.ru's official numbers. (2) 'ФО за матч — прогноз сезона по формуле Sports.ru … (вес прогноза — 10 матчей)': the forecast now uses the FBL formula without the bonus. The in-season update uses calibrated weights rateGames=20 / minuteGames=5 (established) and rateGames=30 / minuteGames=2 (newcomers); PRIOR_GAMES=10 applies only when minutes are missing. (3) 'Ожидаемые ФО = … × доля матчей, которые игрок обычно играет … (не играет — 0, под вопросом — 50%)' omits the hazard chain (chainCurve) that replaced the flat share for players with hazards. (4) ACCEPTANCE says the scoring audit covered '78,901 games, 0 mismatches', but public/data/scoring-audit.json says auditedGames=78714. That audit also only checks the formula against itself (audit_scoring.py:30-31 compares full(row) with the same expression), not against Sports.ru.
evidence: data/inseason-calibration.json points: established {rateGames:20, minuteGames:5, minuteHalfLife:20}, newcomer {rateGames:30, minuteGames:2, minuteHalfLife:5}. season.js:84 uses PRIOR_GAMES only without minutes. scoring-audit.json: auditedGames 78714, checkedAt 2026-10-20T12:18. An actual external check is possible: Sports.ru season totals vs formula + bonus (2023-24..2025-26) match exactly for 86/200, 75/221 and 163/338 players (mean |Δ| 0.86/1.2/0.85 FP per season), and per game Jokic 2025-26 matches 65/65.
impact: The user reads FBL points labelled as Sports.ru's official ones (they differ by about ±1 FP/game per club) and gets a wrong description of how fast estimates react. The '0 mismatches' claim suggests an external validation that never happened.
fix: Relabel as 'очки FBL (Sports.ru без бонуса за результат)'. State the calibrated weights (20/30 games for points per minute, 5/2 for minutes) and the availability chain. Correct the count in ACCEPTANCE. Replace or add to the tautological audit a Sports.ru check: per-season sums from sports-fantasy-history and per game from the game tables.

title: The Sports.ru-week fallback counts free pre-season transfers made on 20.10
claim: transferWeek returns null only for days before the first game week. Week 1 starts on 2026-10-20 (BOS@DET tips at 22:00 MSK that day), so every free pre-season deal of 20.10 (before countFrom 21:30) counts in Sports.ru week 1. transfersThisWeek does not apply isFreeTransfer.
evidence: replay.mjs on the live journals: team 0 Sports.ru-week count is 8 on 2026-10-20, 10-21 and 10-25, while fblTransfers.used is 0 (all 8 deals are 'free'). Fallback: leftOf/transfersLeft = max(0, 3−8) = 0. record() gives used = max(8, 0) = 8, which would show the confirm 'будет 9 трансферов … при лимите 3'.
impact: Only matters when Sports.ru's own transfersLeft is missing (profile layout change, unconnected team). Then team 0 would show 0 transfers left for all of week 1 and get a false limit warning.
fix: In transfersThisWeek, filter out deals where isFreeTransfer is true (or seenAt < countFrom) before counting.

title: Week boundaries come from the last game date of each week number: weeks 7/8 are wrong now and a postponed game would break the ranges; the calendar has 80 of 82 games
claim: Every club calendar lists exactly 80 games: the NBA schedules games 81-82 only after the NBA Cup group stage. US 4-11 Dec therefore has no games, and the derived ranges are week 7 = 12-01..12-04 and week 8 = 12-05..12-14 (10 days). Sports.ru's real week 7 most likely runs to 12-07. Also, a postponed game that keeps its original week number pushes that week's end past the next weeks, giving start>end. The 'До конца сезона' horizon misses 2 games per player.
evidence: Live data: games per club min=max=80. weekOf('2026-12-05') = week 8 {start 12-05, end 12-14}, and the week horizon on 12-05 runs to 12-14. Synthetic gameWeeks with a week-2 game moved to 11-12 gives {'2':{start:'10-27',end:'11-12'},'3':{start:'11-13',end:'11-09'}}.
impact: The 'Неделя' horizon and the week-sorted package optimizer cover the wrong span on 5-7 Dec. The Sports.ru-week fallback counter misassigns those days. Season forecasts are ~2.5% low for every team uniformly (ranks unchanged, swap season gains ~2.5% too small). This corrects itself once Sports.ru adds the games.
fix: Derive a week from the mode or median of its game dates, or cap it at 7 days and fill gaps with Mon-Sun US (Tue-Mon MSK) weeks. Flag a week whose start is after its end. For the season horizon, add 2 placeholder games per club in the NBA Cup window until the calendar lists 82.

title: Journal identity rests on Sports.ru short names: a rename re-stamps old deals with the current time and the replay drops them
claim: Journal events are compared as (date, side, short name, price). shortName() prefers the static database sportsName (snapshot of 17.10) over anything current. If Sports.ru renames a player (it already uses ad-hoc initials such as 'Дж. Мюррэй' or 'К. Джонсон'; 38 short names are shared, e.g. 3×'Мюррэй', 5×'Джонсон'), the event multiset changes with no new deal. stamp_journal then follows the page and gives the renamed rows seenAt=now, and journalTransfers cannot resolve the new name. Separately, the guards (fewer events = failed parse) cannot detect a paginated journal, where a new row pushes the oldest off the page.
evidence: rename.py on team 6's real journal with 'Уайт'→'Д. Уайт' (18 events before and after): the deals Уоглер→Уайт (seenAt 08:03:30Z) and Уайт→Уоглер (08:46:42Z) are re-stamped to 2026-10-22T20:30Z (23:30 MSK). rename.mjs: allTransfers then warns 'куплен Д. Уайт, игрок не найден в базе' and 'продан Д. Уайт, но его нет в составе' and drops both deals. Current data has 0 name mismatches between roster JSON, DB and journal, and the journal page has 18 rows with no pager, so pagination is unconfirmed.
impact: Currently latent. If triggered, deals are dropped from the roster replay (standings and stints wrong, protocols 'На проверке'). If the rows later resolve (database rebuilt with the new name, or pinned ids), the fresh seenAt would turn old daytime deals into 'transfer after 22:00' breaches and free pre-season deals into counted ones.
fix: Key pinned rows by sportsId (sellSid/buySid) in events. Detect a rename as same date/side/price with a changed name and a sportsId match through the roster JSON, and keep the old stamps. Resolve names against the live roster JSON names rather than the 17.10 snapshot. Keep the union of stored dates that vanish from the page instead of dropping them.

title: A ∞ transfer flag from pre-season never clears between full collections
claim: apply() copies the previous team entry and dict.update()s it with parse_team(). parse_team sets transfersUnlimited only when it sees ∞ and never sets it to False. So once a snapshot has transfersUnlimited=True, numeric reads in the minute watcher keep it True until the next full collection rebuilds the entry.
evidence: sticky.py: previous entry {transfersUnlimited:True}, profile 'Трансферы2' gives {'balance':300,'transfersLeft':2,'transfersUnlimited':True}.
impact: For up to 2 h the UI ignores Sports.ru's counter (Infinity, so only the FBL limit applies) and Telegram prints '∞ (предсезонье)'. Current data shows 3 rather than ∞, so the exposure is small.
fix: In parse_team, always set transfersUnlimited (True or False), or pop it when a number is read.

title: Two numbers the league depends on are not observable in the data the app uses: the Yahoo participation term, and an audit trail of the watcher's timestamps
claim: (1) The league scores on Yahoo, whose categories contain GP but no minutes, so the FBL participation term (+2 for 10+ minutes, else +1) cannot be computed from Yahoo totals. Either the league uses c·GP, or the app's formula is not what decides the standings. (2) Breach verdicts on transfer hours rest on seenAt/seenAfter, but the data/season-live branch is re-created with git init and force-pushed every run, so no history of those stamps exists for a dispute.
evidence: 2025-26 logs: games under 10 minutes are 0.6% of top-80 and 1.2% of top-160 player-games, so c=2 changes almost nothing, but c=1 would shift every player by −1 FP/game. 'git log origin/data/season-live' shows 3 commits (12:34-12:40Z 20.10). The 18.10 draft rows of team 0 carry seenAt 07:34-07:37Z 20.10 and their origin cannot be traced.
impact: Possible uniform offset of the season totals. Protocols with 'breach' verdicts cannot be re-audited after the fact.
fix: Ask the league how GP enters the formula, and store the Yahoo-category totals per game (see the box-score finding). Push the live branch without -f, or append a log of journal stamps (date, events, seenAfter, seenAt) to a durable file.

title: Season 80% range is not exchangeable across seasons: held-out coverage 74.6% (15.1% above), production construction (healthy chain) drops to ~70%, yet the UI says '8 seasons out of 10'
claim: The per-tail scale comes from the 0.9 quantile of normalised scores pooled over the six seasons 2020-2025, with leave-one-season-out calibration. That only guarantees coverage if seasons are exchangeable, and they are not. On the held-out 2025-26 season the upper tail needed a scale of 1.106. The model used 0.778, and every one of the six calibration seasons had its own upper q90 between 0.744 and 0.899, so a pooled quantile cannot cover a season like 2026. The misses are concentrated in fringe and short-record players. Production also builds a different interval from the one that was calibrated and tested: it uses healthy=True chains anchored to ESPN games and an averaged ESPN/model rate. The scales were calibrated on unconditional chains anchored to the model mean, so the deployed ranges are narrower than the validated ones. The (n+1) finite-sample correction is not the problem (see verifiedCorrect).
evidence:
Script audit/models-projection-ranges-rookies-slots/exp1.py reproduces run() (scales 1.1982 / 0.7782 match the report), then an1.py:
- Pool seasons after calibration: coverage 0.785 / 0.837 / 0.780 / 0.785 / 0.800 / 0.811. Their own q90 of the upper score: 0.899 / 0.747 / 0.744 / 0.784 / 0.763 / 0.805.
- TEST 2026: below 0.103, above 0.151, cover 0.746. The scale actually needed: low 1.206, high 1.106.
- Subgroups on 2026: rate<10 n=244, cover 0.672 (above 0.209). Evidence <100 games n=161, cover 0.702 (above 0.224). Top-160 by centre, cover 0.794.
- Production construction on the 296 players who played their club's opener (healthy_mean plus healthy=True chain, as apply() does): cover 0.770 -> 0.699 (below 0.041 -> 0.115), mean width 778 -> 676. Top-160 of these: 0.831 -> 0.781.
- Mondrian conformal by record length (exp2.py): interval score 1081 -> 1072. Small gain, and it does not fix the 2026 upper tail.
impact: Every season range shown or simulated (seasonFloor/seasonCeiling, the team simulation, riskAdjustedValue, the rookie timing study and season.js pointsSpread) carries an 80% probability claim that measured about 75% held out, about 67-70% for cheap or short-record players (the waiver and breakout pool), and about 70% under the deployed healthy-chain construction. The ceilings of breakout candidates are too low.
fix: (1) Calibrate the scales on the construction production uses. In the LOSO loop, build the healthy=True chain anchored at healthy_mean for cases that start healthy, the same way as apply(). (2) Treat seasons as the exchangeable unit: take a high quantile of the per-season scales (block conformal), or give recent seasons more weight, and report average width next to coverage, as SCORING_AUDIT.md:28 promises. (3) Use Mondrian calibration by evidence/rate group. (4) Until (1)-(3) are done, replace 'в 8 сезонах из 10' with the measured coverage (about 3 in 4) and give it per group. Measure with the Winkler interval score and per-season coverage on LOSO plus the held-out season.

title: Rookie season ranges use one pooled relative-error set for all picks: every drafted rookie gets a ceiling of 2.1-2.5x his mean (AJ Dybantsa 1052 -> 2211), drafted coverage measures 60-76%, and the UI calls the range 'проверенные на прошлых сезонах'
location: scripts/projection_model.py:240-249, scripts/projection_model.py:548, scripts/projection_model.py:593, src/main.js:235, src/simulation.js:142-150, src/rookie-timing.js:41
claim: Rookie.interval applies the relative rate residuals of all 113 players in the 2025 class to every rookie, with no conditioning on pick. More than half of those residuals belong to undrafted and second-round players, whose predicted rates are about 4-5 FP/G, so their relative errors reach +144% at p90. Multiplying the #1 pick's 14.6 FP/G by those errors gives a ceiling near 30 FP/G for a rookie. These ranges were never checked out of sample: the residuals come from the same class they are meant to describe. A three-class check (fit on class A, take residuals from class B, predict class C, which is the production recipe one class earlier) gives 60-76% coverage for drafted rookies and 87-92% for undrafted ones.
evidence:
rookie6.py on current code:
- Relative residuals, all players: p90 +1.28. By group: picks 1-14 p90 +0.78, picks 15-30 +0.32, undrafted +1.44.
- Interval for pick 1 at ESPN 14.6 x 72: [317, 2208] (0.30x..2.10x). Pick 5: [162, 1465] (2.26x). Pick 12: 2.38x. Pick 30: 2.53x.
- Deployed database: Dybantsa 1052 [317, 2211], Boozer 1009 [304, 2119].
- The best first season among the 2024-26 top-5 picks was 1384 (19.8 x 70). The next best were 1351 and 1133.
- rookie5.py (corrected rows, three-class tests): drafted coverage 0.746, 0.763 and 0.603. Undrafted coverage 0.917, 0.875 and 0.909.
- In the team simulation's two-piece normal, Dybantsa's median becomes (1052 - 0.3113 x 2528) / 0.3774 = 702.
impact: These ranges feed the team simulation, the rookieUpside/veteranUpside scenarios of the rookie timing study, riskAdjustedValue and transfer spreads. Every FBL roster holds a rookie, and five of the eight rostered rookies are top-10 picks with inflated ceilings, which skews each team's simulated distribution. The UI label claiming past-season validation is false for rookies.
fix: Condition the residuals on pick: take the k nearest picks in log(pick), as predict() already does for stat lines, or use additive per-game residuals per pick group. Fit across three or more classes (the 2023-24 league file allows the 2023 class). Validate coverage with the A->B->C scheme above. Label rookie ranges 'не проверено' until they cover.

title: Production season centre and games range rest on unvalidated ESPN games, on average 8.8 games above the validated model (+117 FP per season, +190 for the top 100)
claim: Production replaces the model's games with ESPN's projection for 313 players and anchors the games pmf at ESPN's mean with a healthy start. The comment's reason ('the absence chain predicts too few games for players who start healthy') contradicts the project's own held-out check: the healthy-start shift has a bias of -0.66 games (MAE 13.36). Among the top 160, the healthy shift already over-predicts by 1.8 games. On the same players ESPN sits on average 8.8 games higher than that validated model. Historical totals point the same way: the top 100 by forecast in 2025-26 played 57.0 games, while ESPN projects 70.3 for the top 100 in 2026-27. If ESPN is as optimistic as its gap to the model, the UI statement 'С вероятностью 80% сыграет X-Y матчей' would hold about 64% of the time.
evidence:
Deployed default-draft.json, 300 ESPN-combined players with a chain:
- ESPN games minus model (healthy-adjusted) games: mean +8.8, median +8.1. Mean ESPN 67.2, model 58.4.
- Season FP effect: mean +117, top-100 by FP/G +190.
- exp1.json: 2025-26 top-100/200/300 by centre actually played 57.0 / 57.8 / 55.7 games.
- games1.py on the 296 opener players:
  - unconditional chain: games 80% coverage 0.868
  - healthy chain (production without ESPN): 0.824
  - healthy chain anchored 8.8 games higher: 0.642 (below 0.321), width 28.3 games
- Held-out healthyStart from the report: healthyStartBias -0.656.
impact: meanSeason, slotSeason, the ranges and short-season risk of 313 players, including nearly all of the draftable pool. A systematic games inflation of +9 games favours players ESPN treats as durable and narrows their ranges. The replaced games, and so the slot credits, fall for the same players.
fix: Combine games the same way as the rate (an average or inverse-variance blend of ESPN and the healthy-start model), or keep ESPN games but widen the pmf to the model's dispersion. Archive ESPN projections from now on, so their bias can be measured on 2026-27 and the blend weight fitted. Remove or correct the comment's claim.

title: Rookies drafted in earlier years who debut now get the undrafted model (Thomas Sorber, 2025 #15: 88 FP instead of 374)
claim: apply() reads the draft pick only when DRAFT_YEAR == 2026, and the name fallback draft_names covers only the 2026 class. A player drafted earlier who never played in the NBA therefore falls to UNDRAFTED_ROOKIE_MODEL: 17.1 games and 5.16 FP/G under current code. The official index (data/official-nba-player-index.json) has the correct DRAFT_YEAR and DRAFT_NUMBER as integers.
evidence:
Catalog query: UNDRAFTED_ROOKIE_MODEL players whose official index lists a draft:
- Thomas Sorber (2025 #15, price 1100)
- Bogoljub Markovic (2025 #47)
- Khalifa Diop (2022 #39)
- Tarik Biberovic (2023 #56)
Production Rookie fit (rookie4.py, PIPELINE section): pick 15 gives 7.70 FP/G x 48.6 games = 374 FP; undrafted gives 5.16 x 17.1 = 88 FP. Sorber's season is understated by 286 FP (-76%).
impact: Four rostered rookies (three price 1000, one 1100) carry wrong forecasts, slot values and ranges. A lottery pick looks like a two-way player in transfer advice and rookie boards.
fix: Use official.get('DRAFT_NUMBER') whenever DRAFT_YEAR is set, whatever the year. Build draft_names from all classes in nba-drafts.json. Optionally add a 'years since draft' term, or flag older picks such as Diop's 2022 #39 as low-confidence.

title: Rookie training rows are contaminated: name mismatches count played picks as 0-game picks and again as undrafted rookies, and returning veterans and earlier picks count as undrafted debutants
claim: rookie_rows matches draft names to league logs by normalised name. Unmatched picks are recorded as 0 games, and the same players then reappear as undrafted debutants with their real stats (a double count). nba-drafts.json holds HTML entities ('Nikola Topić', 'Nikola Djurisić'). The 'earlier' set covers only the league files from 2023-24 on, and the 'later' set covers only draft years y-1 and y. As a result, veterans returning after missing 2023-24 and players drafted in earlier classes are counted as undrafted debutants.
evidence:
rookie1.py, rookie2.py, rookie3.py:
- 2024 class: 8 'zero-game' picks, of which Ron Holland II (#5, 81 g), Osasere/Oso Ighodaro (#40, 61 g) and Cam Christie (#46, 12 g) actually played; all three also appear as undrafted rows.
- 2025 class: Yang Hansen (#16) recorded as 0 games, and 'Hansen Yang' played 43.
- The 72 'undrafted' rows of the fit class include 18 players with earlier NBA seasons (Lonzo Ball, Steven Adams, Kevin Porter Jr., Yabusele, Payton, Okafor and others) and 16 picks from earlier classes. The test class has 3 and 4.
- rookie4.py, corrected rows:
  - undrafted share 0.208 -> 0.163 (17.1 -> 13.4 games, 88 -> 68 FP)
  - drafted games +2 to +4 (pick 3: 68.6 -> 72.3)
  - holdout share MAE 0.199 -> 0.174
impact: Rookie levels and residuals (and so the ranges and short-season risk) are biased: undrafted rookies are over-projected by about 20 FP per season and drafted rookies under-projected by 2-4 games. The ACCEPTANCE claim of 'complete draft classes' is not met.
fix: Unescape HTML in names and add an alias table, or better, match by ID (the index's DRAFT_YEAR/NUMBER, or ESPN draftAthleteId). Exclude anyone with an earlier NBA regular-season game in career_games.parquet, and anyone drafted in any earlier class. Add a test that no player is both drafted and undrafted.

title: Replacement level for slot value: 0.874 is a one-game probability, not 'a healthy player's chance to play', and ranks 17-24 do not match the real post-draft free-agent market
claim: The level multiplies by (1 - chain.short - chain.long) = 0.874, the probability that an available player plays the next game. Over a replaced window (12.9 games on average after the 2-game delay), the chain gives a games-weighted availability of 0.724 for a healthy pickup, so this factor overstates the level by 20.7%. The 'ranks 17-24 after 16 starters' premise also fails in the real league: under the cap and human choices only 10-15 of the top 16 per position were drafted. For every one of the 72 rostered players with a credit, the best healthy free agent affordable with his own price plus the team bank is 2.6-8.4 FP/G above replacementPerGame. The two errors roughly cancel today (18.7 x 0.724 = 13.5 against the model's 13.3), but for wrong reasons, and the cancellation will fail once the free-agent pool thins. The model also ignores the replacement's own availability, price feasibility, transfer-budget use (about 2 transfers per long absence, roughly 40 of about 75 a season) and buy-back risk.
evidence:
slot2.py:
- League hazards per available game: short 0.0975, long 0.0285, so 1 - hs - hl = 0.874.
- A healthy pickup's expected share of games: 0.874 over 1 game, 0.769 over 10, 0.734 over 20. Games-weighted over replaced windows: 0.724.
slot1.py with live-sports-current.json rosters:
- Top-16 by FP/G actually rostered: PG 15, SG 10, SF 12, PF 12, C 13.
- Un-rostered free agents include Embiid 22.6, Zion 19.8, Herro 18.8 and Fox 18.1.
- Best affordable healthy FA minus model level: mean +5.37, median +5.06, min +2.61, max +8.41 FP/G (n=72).
impact: Shifts transfer.value and slotSeason for 418 players (mean credit 159.5, max 783 FP), and through them draftValue, riskAdjustedValue and the team simulation. The method claim in the docs is false, and the held-out check cannot catch it because R is the same on both sides.
fix: Compute the level per team from the live un-rostered pool: free agents at the same position, healthy now, price <= sold price + bank, multiplied by the window availability from the chain (or the replacement's own chain). Recompute it from collected rosters each run. Optionally make the delay depend on the transfer budget (3 per week, out and back).

title: The replacement credit is added as a constant while the player's own season varies, so slot downside is understated and injury-prone players are double-penalised
claim: Replacement points rise exactly when the player's own games fall, so the slot season (own + replacement) is far less variable than the own season. scenarioSeasonScore draws the own season from the full range and adds E[transfer.value] as a constant. riskAdjustedValue ranks by slotSeason but subtracts a downside built from the own seasonFloor. Both treat the injury risk as uncovered, which is the risk the slot credit exists to cover.
evidence:
slot3.py, a Monte Carlo of the absence chain with deployed hazards, 20k seasons (format: player: own SD -> slot SD; slot P10 vs own-P10 + E[rep]):
- Jakob Poeltl: 285 -> 117; 861 vs 599
- Brandon Ingram: 313 -> 151; 992 vs 740
- Donte DiVincenzo: P10 618 vs 765
For Poeltl the extra penalty in riskAdjustedValue is about 0.14 x ((792 - 374) - (1018 - 861)) = 37 FP.
impact: Team-simulation win probabilities are flattened for rosters with injury-prone players, and the balanced/best styles over-penalise exactly the players whose risk the slot credit is meant to neutralise.
fix: In Ranges.raw, compute each scenario's replaced games from its games draw (replaced(g) for the scenario's g) and the slot scenario rate*(1+rel)*g + R*replaced(g). Publish slotFloor/slotCeiling and use them in riskAdjustedValue and scenarioSeasonScore instead of own range plus a constant.

title: Season centre is biased high in every season 2020-2026 (2025-26: -41 FP per player, top 160: -72 FP), although the Ranges docstring says the held-out season shows no level bias
claim: Ranges removes each pool season's median error and justifies this as 'a level bias of the survivor-selected older fits, which the held-out 2025-26 season does not show'. The held-out season does show it: the median relative rate error is -6.2%, the median season error -56.5 and the mean -40.8 FP per player, with games over-predicted by 2.9. The mean season error is negative in all seven forward seasons. A likely cause is that the least-squares share regression is fitted on the last six target seasons, which include the survivor-selected career-log seasons before 2024, while the levels use only RECENT = 3.
evidence:
an2.py, mean season error (actual - centre) per season 2020..2026: -18.5, -48.8, -103.9, -60.4, -65.7, -59.9, -40.8. Median relative rate error per season: -0.045 .. -0.107 (2026: -0.062).
On 2026: share error mean -0.036 (-2.94 games). Top-160 by centre: season bias -71.5, games -2.45. Established players (180+ games of evidence): -113 FP, games -5.49. Players with <10 games of evidence: rate over-predicted by 3.92 FP/G (n=18).
impact: The 500 CAREER_MODEL forecasts, and the model half of the 313 combined forecasts, are about 5% too high in level. The ranking between groups is distorted: for example 40-100-game players have a bias of +48 against -113 for established players on 2026 (the age pattern is not stable across seasons). The claim in the docstring is false.
fix: Fit the share regression only on complete-population seasons (2024 onward), or add a season-provenance indicator. Check the out-of-sample mean bias per season as a publishing gate. Remove or correct the docstring sentence.

title: Stale or false method claims in the docs, comments and UI about slot value and ranges
claim:
Several published numbers no longer match current main:
- valuation.js and ACCEPTANCE:165 say 'the top 40 by it produced 1.8% more (top 80: 0.6%)'. On current main (team bonus removed) the figures are top-40 +0.38% and top-80 +1.24%, so the claim was not robust.
- ACCEPTANCE:165 also says '485 players, slot MAE 186 vs 323'.
- ACCEPTANCE:119 says '72% … median floor 39% … Brier 0.094 vs 0.097'.
- projection_model.py:517 says 'Calibration players are held out of the model fit (by player…)'. No player split exists; calibration is temporal.
- SCORING_AUDIT.md:28 promises finite-sample split-conformal padding and width reporting; width is not reported.
- 'Ranks what slots actually produced' overclaims: the 'actual slot' target is built with the same R and delay rule as the predictor. The only direct check, expected against actual replaced games, has Spearman 0.37 with expected 12.5% low.
evidence:
slot4.py on current code:
- Top-40 slot points 58549 -> 58770 (+0.38%), top-80 106969 -> 108293 (+1.24%). The deployed audit from the previous main had +1.75% and +0.62%.
- Report: players 484, slot MAE 320.4 -> 184.6, coverage 0.746, medianFloorShare 0.243, Brier 0.133 vs 0.158.
- Spearman(expected replaced, actual replaced) 0.368. Means 20.32 vs 23.22. Calibration slope 1.09.
impact: Users and the owner are shown validation numbers that the code no longer produces, and the evidence for the slot ranking is weaker than stated.
fix: Generate these numbers from the audit JSON at build time instead of hard-coding them. Correct the comment at line 517. Report the direct replaced-games calibration and the average interval width. Describe the slot check as a test of the absence model under the assumed replacement rule.

title: Rookie share model forecasts 82 games for every #1 pick, and its pick slope is unstable with one or two draft classes
claim: The share regression is linear in log(pick) with intercept at or above 1.0, so share is clipped to 1.0 at pick 1: 82 games in every class fit. In 2023-2025 the top-3 picks played 52-75 games, 68.2 on average. The rate slope also swings from -1.79 to -3.17 between single classes (SE about 0.5). The pipeline ignores the 2023 class, although the 2023-24 league file is available.
evidence:
rookie7.py: every class fit gives pick1 x 82 games. Picks 1-3 by class: (71, 74, 62), (75, 66, 52), (70, 69, 75). Rate slope:
- 2023 class: -3.17
- 2024 class: -1.79 (the class used for the holdout fit)
- 2025 class: -3.00
- 2024+2025: -2.39 (SE 0.34)
- 2023+2024+2025: -2.64 (SE 0.29)
The UI shows the model as 'модель новичков (пик №1): 14.4 × 82 матча' (main.js:224, sources.model.games = 82 for Dybantsa).
impact: Inflates the #1 pick's model games by about 14 (about 200 FP), as shown in the source line and used whenever ESPN is missing. The swing between classes drives pick-1 forecasts from 11.9 to 16.2 FP/G.
fix: Use a logit or beta link for share, pool three or more classes (2023-24 via the league file, with career logs for the debut check), and add class random effects. Validate by leaving one class out.

title: Game floor and ceiling of 12 rostered players come unshifted from the previous pipeline's role prior, while the UI calls them the player's own 90th percentile
claim: When a player has a career record but fewer than 10 games in the last two seasons, game_floor and game_ceiling keep the previous forecast's values (from complete_forecasts, whose own gameRangeBasis says 'NOT a calibrated game P90'). The calibrated game_ratios path runs only if those values are None, and the old values are not shifted to the new rate.
evidence:
gf2.py: 12 SOURCE_REPORTED players. Deployed versus game_spread (floor/ceiling):
- Vladislav Goldin: 2.2 / 17.7 vs -0.5 / 13.8
- Chris Manon: 2.9 / 18.0 vs 0.0 / 14.6
- Alex Morales: 0.3 / 17.8 vs 0.0 / 15.1
Mean ceiling difference +1.13.
impact: A few fringe, low-price players show game ceilings 3-4 FP too high, and season.js per-game spreads use them.
fix: Use game_ratios(rate) whenever len(logs) < 10, or shift the inherited values by rate - f['meanPerGame'].

title: Rookies get no replacement credit, so they are biased against veterans in draftValue
claim: slotSeason adds the replacement credit only for players with an NBA record. Veterans' DNP-CD spells are in the absence chain too, and the rookie rule binds only one rookie per roster, so an extra rookie can be swapped like anyone else.
evidence: Deployed: veterans with 40-55 forecast games average a credit of 259 FP (n=45) against 0 for 16 rookies. At 70-83 games: 65 FP against 0 (13 rookies).
impact: Small for standings now (each FBL team holds exactly one rookie), but it biases rookie-against-veteran comparisons in recommendations and the rookie timing study by up to about 260 FP.
fix: Credit a rookie with replacement by another rookie (the rookie-level replacement) when he is the roster's only rookie, and with the normal level otherwise. Or apply the chain-free credit R x max(0, 82 - games - delay x spells) at a discounted rate.

title: Range pairing uses one fixed permutation: Monte Carlo noise of about 5% of the centre on the ceiling, and the rate/games independence assumption is contradicted by the data
claim: Ranges.games shuffles the 150 games quantiles with random.Random(150), the same permutation for every player, and takes P10/P90 of 150 products. The exact mixture CDF, (1/n)·Σ_i P(G ≤ s/(rate(1+rel_i))), is cheap and deterministic. Separately, rate errors and games errors correlate positively in every season, against the docstring's independence. A joint PIT pairing that keeps this dependence did not improve held-out interval scores once the conformal scaling was applied.
evidence:
perm1.py, 40 players: SD of P90 over 30 permutations 5.4% of centre (max 13.2%); P10 2.5%. Fixed permutation against the exact mixture: mean |dP90| 3.9% of centre.
an2.py, corr(rel rate error, games error) per season 2020..2026: 0.216, 0.162, 0.392, 0.348, 0.434, 0.266, 0.341.
exp2.py, held-out 2026 interval score: independent 1081, joint 1102.
impact: Arbitrary ±50 FP jitter on the ceiling of a 1000-FP player, and a documented assumption that is false (harmless after calibration).
fix: Replace the shuffled pairing with exact mixture quantiles over the full pmf. Document the measured dependence. If dependence is modelled later, judge it by interval score, not coverage alone.

title: season.js pointsSpread uses the season-total range, which includes games and injury risk, as a per-game level uncertainty for transfer confidence
claim: rel = (seasonCeiling - seasonFloor)/(2·Z90·meanSeason) is multiplied by horizon points that already contain expected games, so availability uncertainty is counted in both rel and the play rate. For CAREER_MODEL players the season range is dominated by the games spread.
evidence: Deployed top 250 by FP/G, implied relative SD: ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED median 0.29 (p90 0.41), CAREER_MODEL median 0.44 (p90 0.64). The rate-only spread from the pooled neighbour errors is about 0.27, from an2 p10/p90 ≈ -0.45/+0.25.
impact: Swap confidence (normalCdf(gain/sd) against CONFIDENT = 0.7) is understated when a career-model player is involved, so some valid transfers are labelled DOUBTFUL.
fix: Publish a rate-only P10/P90 (the rel quantiles of the neighbours times rate) and use it for horizon spreads. Treat games uncertainty through playRate.

title: Missing birth dates (25% of training rows, almost all players who left the league) remove the age effect and push every veteran forecast up

title: Season totals are systematically over-predicted (-41 FP on the holdout, -44 to -66 in forward seasons) and the report shows no bias metric; the share regression mixes survivor seasons and uses a U-shaped age term
claim:

title: For 313 ESPN-covered players, games, season totals, games ranges and short-season risk come from ESPN's games (8.9 above the validated model); the 'checked on 2025/26' label does not apply to them
claim: apply() sets games=espn['games'] for ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED players. The stated reason is that the absence chain predicts too few games for players who start healthy, but the healthy-start shift added since then is almost unbiased (healthyStartBias -0.66 over 296 players). with_games() then scales the chain hazards to ESPN's mean, so gamesRange, shortSeasonRisk and the conformal season range (calibrated on model errors) all centre on an unvalidated number. ESPN's mean is 67.4 games against the model's 58.5 (+8.9, median +8.2). On 2025/26, the top-313 players by model rate played 53.0 games, and those who played their club's first game played 60.2. Only 34.5% (43.7% for healthy starters) reached 67 games. The forecast basis text still says the weights were fitted on seasons up to 2024/25 and checked on 2025/26 ('веса модели подобраны ... проверены на 2025/26') for these players, whose games and range were never tested.
evidence:
Deployed public/data/default-draft.json: 313 ESPN players, mean ESPN games 67.4 vs sources.model.games 58.5; ESPN per game +0.33 FP over the model. Examples: Max Strus 67 vs 33.4, Grant Williams 63 vs 43.2, Zach Collins 56 vs 33.4, Bronny James 63 vs 46.1, Coby White 72 vs 55.0. Nickeil Alexander-Walker: games 79, gamesRange [75,82], shortSeasonRisk 0.002.
e9_games.py: 2025/26 top-313 actual 53.0 games (model 54.6); 231 healthy starters actual 60.2.
e22_espn_games.py on those 231 players: chain anchored to the model's healthy-start mean gives 80% games-range coverage 84.4%, bias +0.89, short risk 4.9% (actual 4.3%). Anchored to model+8.9 (ESPN-like): coverage 61.0% (36.4% below the range), bias +9.76, short risk 2.3% against 4.3% actual.
impact: Season totals (meanSeason, slotSeason), games ranges and injury-risk numbers for the 313 most relevant players are probably about 7-9 games (12-15%) too optimistic. ESPN players are also systematically favoured over the 143 CAREER_MODEL players in season-total rankings (ranks 100-250 hold 34 model-only against 116 ESPN players). Label ESPN-combined ranges as uncalibrated. Score the frozen ESPN snapshot against 2026/27 games after about 20 games and set the weight by a forward fit.

Top-50 and bottom tiers are near zero or positive. Decomposition (e6c, e18): mostly minutes over-predicted, by 0.6-1.5 min, plus per-minute error of -0.2 to -0.3 FP. It is worst for ages 29+ (-0.88 FP/g, -1.52 min) and for players without a birth date (-2.97 FP/g). The overall calibration slope is about 1, so a single global statistic hides it.

Then add an out-of-sample recalibration layer: isotonic or kernel smoothing of the residual against predicted rate, fitted on the last two forward seasons and applied before the ESPN blend. Report tier-wise games-weighted bias in the audit JSON and test it, for example |bias| < 0.4 FP/g for ranks 50-250 on 2026.

title: The 'untouched' 2025/26 holdout was used for model selection, so the published 95% gain, coverage and Brier are optimistic
claim: Several design choices were scored on the season the report calls untouched. FRAILTY=2.5, decay 0.6 and the 2400/640 priors were chosen forward on 2021-2026 by log score, which includes 2026. The share regression replaced the shrinkage because it won forward-tested 2020-2026. A minutes-dependent shrink target was rejected because it 'lost on the held-out season'. Team-minute scaling was 'not adopted' on held-out minutes. Each look at the test season is a fork; repeated looks make the reported pairedGain95 [13.6, 36.7], gamesCoverage80 0.80 and shortSeasonBrier 0.133 conditionally biased toward success. The docstring line 15 says 'Test: 2025-26 (untouched)'.

impact: The headline holdout numbers on the audit page and in ACCEPTANCE overstate how reliable the method is. The real out-of-sample check is the 2026/27 season.
fix: Freeze every hyperparameter on seasons up to 2025 (refit FRAILTY, decay and priors on 2021-2025, record selection choices made on ≤2025 data) and keep 2026 as a single final check. Or report a nested scheme: select on 2021-2024, test on 2025, then on 2026. Pre-register the 2026/27 evaluation with the frozen 17 Oct snapshot.

title: Earlier-drafted debutants get the undrafted-rookie model (Thomas Sorber #15 forecast at 17 games)

title: Participation term: the hard-coded logistic over-predicts sub-10-minute games for bench players; Yahoo scoring has no minutes category
claim: E[bonus] = 2 - P(min<10) is the correct expectation of the FBL formula. But the prior prior_short = 1/(1+exp((min-8)/2.5)) is not fitted, and with only 10 games of weight it dominates for players whose minutes change. Separately, data/league-rules.json says Yahoo keeps standings from the categories GP, FGA, FGM, FTA, FTM, PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK, TO, PF, with no minutes, and that 'the league counts them with the FBL formula'. If points are computed from Yahoo totals, the 10-minute threshold cannot be applied (it would have to be per GP), which changes the participation term by P(min<10) per game.

e2_bias.py, 2026 holdout, games-weighted short fraction by predicted minutes:
- 8-12 min: predicted 0.603, actual 0.442 (n 49).
- 12-16 min: 0.378 vs 0.275 (n 82).
