There are no rows under 1 minute in 2023-24 (239 and 194 in the other two seasons), so cameo games are lost. 2024-25 has 1,223 of 1,230 games (missing 0022400524, 532, 537, 538, 617, 627, 988; 11 teams with 80-81 games). The impact on forecasts is negligible.
evidence: e23_trunc.py: adding +0.5 min to 2023-24 changes test per-game MAE 2.532→2.532 and production current-player rate by a mean -0.005 (max 0.021 FP/g). Team totals and the ESPN comparison come from inline scripts in this audit.
impact: Negligible for FP forecasts. The minute levels shown (league_min 20.40 vs 20.56) are slightly off; the 10-minute threshold is exact under floor truncation.
fix: Restore the 7 games and the 2023-24 seconds from the NBA stats API, or label 2023-24 as truncated in the minute-encoding report. Optionally add +0.5 min to truncated rows in league_rows().

title: In-season value of an injured player counts his reported absence twice (playRate plus injuryFactor), and again when ESPN's games already include it
claim: expectedPoints zeroes every club game until the ESPN returnDate (injuryFactor) and then scales the post-return chain to share=playRate. But playRate is a per-game Beta-binomial update (k=20) that counts every missed game of the ongoing reported spell as evidence. It was calibrated (inseason_calibration.availability_cases) with no injury information, on the share of all remaining games, so that share already covers the rest of the current spell. Once injuryFactor removes those games, the lowered share is applied a second time, to games after the return. Before the season the same thing happens through the prior: for players ESPN projects with a known long absence (DiVincenzo 4, Sharpe 27, Butler 39, Moody 12 games against model 62/56/44/59), share = games/82 already contains the absence, and the absence is then cut out again until returnDate. In the semi-Markov model one 15-game spell is a single long-spell event and barely moves the hazard posterior (prior weight 640 games).
evidence: Synthetic case with the real functions (scratchpad audit/models-availability-chain/synthetic.mjs): forecast 66 games at 20 FP, 20 club games done, played 5 then missed 15, ESPN Out until club game 25. playRate 0.527 (healthy: 0.902), rest-of-season expected games 31.1. Leaving the spell out of playRate (share 0.844) gives 48.7, the prior 0.805 gives 46.6, so 15.5-17.6 games (310-350 FP) are lost. Empirical check (postreturn.py), 213 returns from spells of 10+ games, single-club players, 2024/25 and 2025/26: share of the remaining season actually played was 0.563. JS playRate at the return was 0.429 (bias -0.135, MAE 0.258); playRate without the spell's games was 0.609 (bias +0.046, MAE 0.211). Live data on 21.10 (inj.mjs), season horizon against forecast games: Butler 25.4 vs 39 (-282 FP), Porzingis 44 vs 59 (-248), Sharpe 12.2 vs 27 (-194), Strawther 51.3 vs 66, Gueye 55.9 vs 70, Claxton 61.6 vs 69, Ingram 48.7 vs 55.
impact: Any injured player, rostered or free agent, has his season and month value understated by 15-35% after the return. This feeds bestTransfers/marketAlerts (gain.season>0 guard), bestPackage protectSeason, transferVerdict and injuredTargets (the 'buy injured before the market reacts' feature), and pushes advice toward selling injured stars. Today no FBL roster holds an Out player, so current advice is unchanged (checked across the 8 teams). It becomes material with the first in-season injury.
fix: In playRate, drop from both `on` and `team` the club games inside an absence the report explains (dates before returnDate while ESPN lists the player Out, or the current run of consecutive misses whenever injuryFactor<1 applies). Alternatively, replace the per-game update with the spell-based posterior already in availability_model (one spell = one event). For the pre-season prior of a player whose forecast games come from ESPN and who has an Out entry, anchor the post-return chain to min(0.97, games/available club games after return) or to the model's healthy-start share, not to games/82. Measure: MAE of the post-return share on the returns of 2024/25-2025/26 (0.258 -> about 0.21).

title: The in-season chain always starts 'available now'; the GTD 0.5 branch never fires, so day-to-day or unreported absent players count as fully available
claim: chainCurve sets p[0]=1 (available) for every player. The elapsed length of the current absence, the state a semi-Markov chain exists to use, is never read from live.games or the club calendar. Only injuryFactor can lower the near-term chance, and its GTD branch is dead in practice. ESPN gives every Day-To-Day player a returnDate equal to the next game's US date, while the calendar is Moscow-dated (US date + 1), so `day<back` is never true and the factor is 1. A player who has missed 3 straight games while listed D2D, or who is absent without any ESPN entry, gets about 86% for his next game.
evidence: tz.mjs on the live data: 0 of 51 GTD players with a calendar get factor 0.5 on their next game. missed2.py, 2025/26 rotation players (pre-season share >= 0.6, >= 20 mpg) who missed their club's last game, 3345 cases. Next-3 played: actual 0.308, JS healthy-start chain 0.793, semi-Markov start from the elapsed run (KM residual p0[r] ∝ hs*fs[d+r]+hl*fl[d+r], same hazards and lengths) 0.316. MAE 0.536 -> 0.274. By elapsed run: after 1 missed game 0.586 actual vs 0.863 JS; 2-3 games 0.376 vs 0.857; 4-9 games 0.214 vs 0.818; 10+ games 0.087 vs 0.663. For Out entries, US vs Moscow dates currently cause no off-by-one (0 of 30 have a game on the Moscow date equal to returnDate), but the comparison is structurally one day off.
impact: Week and month values for D2D players (55 of 90 current ESPN entries) and for unreported absences are overstated by roughly 2.5x on the next games. This distorts weekly transfer choices under the 3-per-week limit and the confidence figures.
fix: Compute the current run d of consecutive missed club games (finished games without a played row) and start chainCurve from p0[r] ∝ hs*shortLengths[d+r]+hl*longLengths[d+r] instead of p[0]=1. Cache by (h,share,d). Treat GTD as a probability (fit it from the injury archive once collected, about 0.6-0.7 as a placeholder) for the next game regardless of returnDate. Compare returnDate with the game's US date (Moscow date - 1). Measure next-3/next-7 MAE on 2025/26 as above.

title: 'Health by the logs' / 'History of absences' shows the hazards after they were scaled to the forecast games, not the player's history
claim: availability.shortSpellsPer82 and longSpellsPer82 are c*hs*82 and c*hl*82, where c is the bisection factor that forces the chain's mean to equal the published games (ESPN's for covered players). The UI calls them 'Здоровье по логам 2002–2026: коротких пропусков X за 82 матча при Y у ровесников' and 'История пропусков'. The personal posterior hazards are almost all age-group prior (prior weights 2400/640 games against about 160 weighted personal games), so the displayed personal number is in effect ESPN's or the model's games re-expressed as absence rates. The peer number beside it is unscaled, so the comparison mixes scaled and unscaled quantities.
evidence: prod.py (production chain, seasons <2027) on 800 players. Unscaled personal short spells per 82, deciles 6.9-8.2; displayed deciles 2.5-29.1; scale c deciles 0.33-3.66 (top-120 by FP/game: 0.0025 to 3.33). Examples: Jokic personal 6.92/1.69, displayed 2.6/0.6 (c=0.38); Giddey 7.95 -> 3.3; Mikal Bridges 6.36/1.35 -> 0.0/0.0 (ESPN 82 games); DiVincenzo shows 174.0 short and 39.9 long absences per 82 games; 67 players show more than 30 short absences per 82.
impact: Every player card and transfer explanation shows invented health-history numbers that read as facts about the logs. Durable-looking or fragile-looking players are labelled by ESPN's games projection instead.
fix: Publish the unscaled posterior (hs, hl from Availability.hazards) as the history, and label the scaled values separately ('spells implied by the forecast of N games'), or drop them. Keep `hazards` (scaled) only for the JS chain.

title: Anchoring the chain to ESPN's games collapses the games distribution for high projections (degenerate [82,82] ranges, about 0% short-season risk)
claim: The chain's mean is forced to equal ESPN's games, which are often 77-82. The only way to get there is to shrink both hazards towards zero (c down to exp(-6)), which also removes almost all variance. ESPN's number is a point projection, not a ceiling, so the resulting gamesRange, shortSeasonRisk and the games scenarios inside the season range (Ranges.games) are overconfident. When the target is above what the chain can reach (GTD players start from the generic distribution), the pmf mean silently stays below the published games.
evidence: From public/data/default-draft.json and prod.py: Mikal Bridges, Julian Champagnie and Bub Carrington (ESPN 82) have gamesRange [82,82] and shortSeasonRisk 0.0. 42 players have hazards scaled below 0.25x, e.g. Amen Thompson 78 -> [72,82] with short risk 0.004, DeRozan 77 -> [70,82] with 0.005. Unattainable targets: Podziemski 79 and Knueppel 78 -> pmf mean 76.8. Empirically (iron.py), of players with 75+ games who played their club's opener the next season, 53.2% (2024/25) and 51.9% (2025/26) played fewer than 72 games, and 25.3% / 22.2% fewer than 60.
impact: Season floors and confidence (pointsSpread uses seasonFloor/Ceiling) are too tight for exactly the players ESPN rates most durable. Transfer confidence is overstated and the short-season warning never fires for them.
fix: Shrink the anchor: target = w*ESPN + (1-w)*chain healthy-start mean at c=1, with w fitted by the log score of actual games, or bound c to [0.5, 3]. Equivalently, treat ESPN's games as a noisy observation of the mean (mixture over c). Check that the holdout PIT is flat for predicted means of 75+.

title: Known long absences are ignored before the season: model-only players keep unconditional games and injured players get a generic start distribution with inflated hazards
claim: apply() uses the ESPN report only as a healthy/not-healthy flag. Injured players get p0 = the league start distribution of their previous-season group, not the known block of games until returnDate. The database stores injuries without returnDate, so the build cannot use it. For CAREER_MODEL players the forecast games stay unconditional. For ESPN-covered injured players the chain is forced to ESPN's low games by inflating per-game hazards, which spreads the absence randomly through the season instead of as one block. That distorts gamesRange, shortSeasonRisk and replacedGames (slot value).
evidence: default-draft.json: Mark Williams (Out to 2027-02-03, labrum surgery) 53.4 games, 928 FP, short risk 8.9%. Jamir Watkins (torn ACL, return 2027-04-02) 50.1 games, 10.9%. Jordan Miller (to 2027-03-02) 50.6 games. Ariel Hukporti (season-ending Achilles) 49 games, 11.4%. Ben Simmons (OFS) 28.1 games, 50.5%. DiVincenzo's exported hazards [2.122, 0.486] per game, with the 0.45 cap binding; replacedGames 56.1 against about 72 club games before an April return. The 0.45 cap binds in some frailty stratum for 225 of 800 players. Holdout analog (holdout.py), 2025/26 players who missed their club's opener (n=188): forecast games biased +14.2, 80% games range covers 68.6%, 28.2% fall below q10.
impact: Player cards, season ranges and the insights warning (shown only at 20%+) are wrong for about 12 model-only injured players and distorted for every ESPN-covered injured player. The playRate prior in season is inflated for the same players.
fix: Keep returnDate and the comment in player.injuries at build time. Set p0 = point mass at the number of club games before returnDate (82 for OFS or season-ending wording), anchor only the post-return part, and use the healthy-start chain after return for model-only players. Validate on the 'missed the opener' holdout group (coverage and bias).

title: playRate floors every prior at 0.5 (41 games) and caps it at 0.97: low-games and rookie forecasts inflated, never validated
claim: prior=clamp(games/82, 0.5, 0.97). The clamp copies the calibration script, but the calibration population only holds players with 20+ games and 10+ mpg in the previous season (prior_of returns None otherwise). The floor was therefore never tested on what production feeds it: rookies, fringe players and long-injured ESPN projections. In production a 16-game forecast becomes about 40 expected games. Rookies without hazards use the flat share, which is floored too.
evidence: Live check (inj.mjs, today 21.10): Blake Hinson forecast 23.7 games -> 40.1 season games expected (+179 FP); Rocco Zikarsky 23 -> 40.1 (+160); Thomas Sorber 17.1 -> 39.5 (+139); Khalifa Diop 17.1 -> 40 (+128); Moses Moody ESPN 12 -> 31 (+209). 60 market players have forecast games < 41 (45 CAREER_MODEL, 6 DRAFT_PICK_MODEL rookies, 5 undrafted rookies, 4 ESPN); approximate inflation up to 220 FP (Chucky Hepburn 16.1 games). Six players with 80-82 games are capped at 79.5. Today's top-3 advice for the 8 teams is unchanged with the floor removed (advice.mjs variants), so the effect is concentrated in fringe and rookie choices.
impact: Cheap fringe players and rookies, the candidates for the rookie rule and budget slots, look about 2x more available than forecast. Market alerts or the rookie choice can favour them wrongly.
fix: Use prior = clamp(g/82, 0.02, 0.99), or a Beta prior with mean g/82. Refit priorGames on a population that includes low-minute players and rookies (the share of remaining games).

title: Mid-season signings, call-ups and players new to a club are charged with every club game played before they arrived
claim: team = max(rows.length, finished, on), where finished counts all of the current club's scored games since opening night. A player signed or called up mid-season, or a free agent picked up later, gets every earlier club game counted as missed. Traded players are measured against the new club's calendar.
evidence: Synthetic, real playRate/expectedPoints: forecast 65 games (prior 0.793), signed after club game 40, played 5 of 5 since -> playRate 0.321, rest-of-season expected games 13.3 of 37 (about 30 under the prior).
impact: Exactly the in-season pickups a manager would consider (newly signed or promoted players) are undervalued by about 60% in transfer advice.
fix: Count team games only from the player's first listed game for his current club (or from the Sports.ru listing date), and use the old club's calendar for games before a trade.

title: The 2019/20 COVID season is rebuilt wrongly: fake 37-game end spells for non-bubble teams contaminate the spell lengths, the start-out rates and the HEALTHY_SHIFT weight
claim: season_games(2020)=72, so the 8 non-bubble teams (ATL, CHA, CHI, CLE, DET, GS, MIN, NY: 64-67 dates, under 0.95*72) fall back to the day-spacing estimate across the March-July 2020 hiatus. Every player who played through 11 March gets a censored end spell of about 37 games. These count as long-spell starts, enter the long KM as censored spells, and mark those players' 2020/21 season as 'endedOut', which feeds the start distribution and the HEALTHY_SHIFT fit. All-Star and Rising Stars games (EAST/WEST/LEB/GIA/STE/DUR/USA/WORLD, 389 rows 2013-2023) are also in the REGULAR career logs.
evidence: covid.py/len.py: 2020 has 52 end spells of exactly 37 games (plus 38-40); 31% of 2020 seasons end out 10+ games against 12-18% in other seasons; rebuilt 2020 length ranges 53-103 (mean 77.4) against 82.0 in 2024-2026. Fixed (season length 63, covid_fix.py): endedOut start-out 39.1% -> 42.9% (ACCEPTANCE claims 38%), long spell mean 14.94 -> 14.16, lump at 82 games 4.58% -> 3.81%, P(len>=20) 0.188 -> 0.178. shift.py, 2021-2025 recomputation: best endedOut weight 0.30 on 170 cases (matches HEALTHY_SHIFT), but 53 of them are 2021 COVID artefacts; without them the weight is 0.60 (played 57.3, unconditional 53.3, healthy chain 62.2).
impact: The shape constants (long-tail length, start-out after an injured ending) are biased, and the endedOut healthy-start shift is about half what the clean data supports: about 2.7 games too few for the 12 model-only endedOut-but-healthy players. The documented 38% start-out is an artefact.
fix: Use per-team calendars for 2020 (or season_games(2020)=63 so 64-67-date calendars count as complete), drop rows whose team is not an NBA franchise, then refit length_pmf, start and HEALTHY_SHIFT.

title: Absence-hazard estimator does not match the chain it feeds (back-to-back spells merge; exposure excludes spell-start states)
claim: counts() treats each run of consecutive misses as one spell and divides by games played. The chain, however, lets a new spell start on the game right after a spell ends (merged in the data), and each spell start uses up an available state (exposure should be games + spells). Fitting on gaps and then simulating the chain does not reproduce the data: short spells come out too rare, long ones too frequent, and the short-length pmf is skewed. Kaplan-Meier itself is implemented correctly.
evidence: km_sim.py: 3000 player-seasons simulated from the chain with true hs=0.08 and hl=0.025, using the app's own KM lengths. The estimators give hs 0.0745 (-7%) and hl 0.0278 (+11%), short:long ratio 2.68 against 3.2. Short pmf P(1,2,3) = 0.597/0.241/0.162 against true 0.646/0.220/0.134. Long KM: mean 15.18 vs 14.94, P(>=20) 0.1889 vs 0.1876, median 7 = 7; naive non-censored estimate 11.88. Unanchored chain on 2025/26: games MAE 19.4 vs regression 17.07, bias +4.97.
impact: Limited by the anchoring: it shifts the short/long mix (shape of the games pmf, replacedGames) by about 10% and biases the reported league rates (7.9/2.3 per 82). It is part of why the chain's own mean loses to the regression.
fix: Make the chain a renewal process: after a spell the next game is played. Or estimate spells and lengths jointly by EM, with exposure = games + spells. Test: simulate, re-estimate, check recovery.

title: Games-range and short-season claims hide a miscalibrated lower tail, and the validated pmf is not the published one
claim: '80% games range covers 79.6%' (now 79.75%) is an aggregate. The inclusive discrete [q10,q90] has a model-nominal coverage of 82.0%, the misses are lopsided (13.4% below, 6.8% above) and the PIT is significantly non-uniform. Short-season risk is under-predicted in the middle bins. evaluate() validates the unconditional pmf anchored to the regression, while production publishes healthy-start pmfs anchored to ESPN games for most players and unconditional pmfs for injured ones. The healthy-start version is well calibrated on the 'played the opener' proxy; the unconditional one fails badly on its analog group.
evidence: holdout.py, 2025/26 (n=484): empirical 79.75%, nominal 82.0%, below 13.4%, above 6.8%. PIT deciles [67,67,39,51,48,49,38,55,35,35], chi2 = 26.8 with 9 df (p about 0.0015). Short risk mean 0.163 vs observed 0.196; bin 0.1-0.2: 0.140 predicted vs 0.231 observed (n=108); bin 0.05-0.1: 0.067 vs 0.095 (n=253). Brier 0.1325 vs base 0.1578 (reproduced). Healthy-start pmf on players who played the opener (n=296): coverage 82.4%, nominal 82.4%, below 9.1%, above 8.4%. Did not play the opener (n=188): 68.6% coverage, 28.2% below, bias +14.2 games.
impact: Users see '80% range' and short-season percentages that are reliable for healthy starters but too optimistic for uncertain or injured players.
fix: Report nominal and empirical coverage per tail with PIT. Recalibrate the unconditional pmf's lower tail (conformal per tail on games, as already done for points). Validate the pmf actually published (healthy flag, ESPN mean) once an ESPN archive exists.

title: seasonEnding misses 'remainder of the season', 'season-ending' and 'entirety of the ... season'; Furphy is valued as back on 2 January
claim: The regex only matches 'out for (the) season' and 'miss the (entire|rest of the|20xx-yy) season'. 'Will miss the remainder of the season', with status OUT and a placeholder returnDate, passes as an ordinary injury, so the player counts as available from returnDate. injuredTargets also uses seasonEnding to skip such players.
evidence: Live ESPN feed and archive: Johnny Furphy, 'torn right ACL ... will miss the remainder of the season', OUT, returnDate 2027-01-02. seasonEnding is false; expectedPoints gives 36.8 season games (about 243 FP at 6.6 FP/game). Hukporti ('season-ending', OUT 2027-10-01), Simmons (OFS) and Oweh ('entirety', OFS) are rescued only by their status or returnDate; for all three the regex misses.
impact: Phantom value for season-ending injuries whose wording ESPN varies. The player can show up as an injured buy target.
fix: Extend the pattern to /season[- ]ending|(remainder|rest|entirety) of the (20\d\d-\d\d )?season|miss the (entire )?(20\d\d-\d\d )?season|out for the (season|year)/i, and treat returnDate after the last calendar date as season-ending. Add test cases from injury-history.json.

title: The documented next-3/7/28 in-season backtest cannot be reproduced and appears anchored to the realized season share
claim: The 86.1/89.3, 83.7/86.4 (MAE 0.194 -> 0.165) and 78.1/81.6 figures with 'season share 78.2%' have no script in the repository. My replication reproduces the pattern only when the chain is anchored to the player's realized 2025/26 share, which is look-ahead. Under the production anchor (playRate from the pre-season share, k=20) the chain still beats the flat share, by less. By the doc's own numbers the chain is worse than the flat share at 28 games (81.6 vs actual 78.1; flat 78.2).
evidence: nextn.py, 2025/26 test players who played their club's last game. Anchored to the realized share: next-3 actual 0.847, chain 0.859, share 0.748; next-7 0.822 / 0.830 / 0.749; next-28 0.772 / 0.786 / 0.753. Production-like anchor: next-7 chain 0.832, actual 0.819, flat playRate 0.742; MAE 0.178 vs 0.209 (n=3637).
impact: The stated gain is an oracle figure. The real gain is smaller but positive.
fix: Commit the backtest script, anchor it to the forecast available at the checkpoint, and report those numbers.

title: Docs and UI still say games are averaged with ESPN; since #61 they are ESPN's alone, and the holdout metrics validate a different quantity
claim: ACCEPTANCE says the chain's mean equals 'the forecast games (regression, or its mean with ESPN)' and that ESPN's games are 'half of the combined mean'. The projection_model docstring says 'its mean set to the regression's'. The code uses ESPN's games alone (#61, not recorded in ACCEPTANCE). forecastSources prints 'модель по карьере: X × M матчей; ESPN: Y × N — итог их среднее', but only the per-game value is averaged. All holdout games metrics (MAE 17.1, coverage, Brier) are for the regression games, not for the ESPN games the app publishes for every covered player.
evidence: git show 22a494a: 'games are ESPN's whenever ESPN projects the player' (no docs change). projection_model.py:587 `games=espn['games'] if espn else model_games`.
impact: Readers think the games mix two sources and that the published games were validated.
fix: Update ACCEPTANCE, the docstring and main.js ('ФО за матч — среднее, матчи — ESPN'), and state that the games of ESPN-covered players are not validated.

title: The 'frailty quadrature' is 7 equal-probability Monte Carlo strata, the JS twin has no frailty, and the 0.45 cap truncates the mixture
claim: The Gamma(2.5) season multiplier is integrated with 7 stratum means of a seeded 70k sample, not a quadrature rule. This loses 10% of the variance (the top stratum mean of 2.18 hides the upper tail). The hazard cap of 0.45 clips the top strata for many fringe players. JS drops frailty entirely; otherwise it is an exact twin.
evidence: curve.py: stratum variance 0.360 vs 0.400; points [0.259 ... 2.179]. JS vs Python without frailty: max abs difference 0.0 on 6 cases. With frailty, next-3 availability differs by up to 2.8pp at share 0.5 (0.711 vs 0.683) and 1pp or less at share >= 0.8. Cap binding in 225 of 800 production players.
impact: Slightly thin lower tail of the games pmf, consistent with the excess of low PIT values. In-season near-term values are slightly too high for low-share players.
fix: Use generalized Gauss-Laguerre nodes and weights for Gamma(2.5,1/2.5) (exact up to polynomial degree 13). Apply the same nodes in JS (7x the work, negligible). Replace the hard cap by a bounded scale.

title: The 'season without games' start-out rate mixes injured players with multi-year non-NBA gaps
claim: The noGames group (74.6% start out) combines 91 returning seasons (61.5% start out) with 47 inner seasons of multi-year gaps (2-5 seasons, typically out of the NBA), each counted as 82 games out. For a rostered player who missed one season injured, the relevant base rate is closer to the returning-season figure. Seasons near the end of the data cannot contribute noGames cases (survivorship).
evidence: nogames.py: returning seasons 91, 56 with start>0 (61.5%); 47 inner missing seasons; run lengths {2:17, 3:12, 4:6, 5:12}; built share 0.746.
impact: Small: only noGames players without a healthy flag use it. In production 211 of them, mostly not on current rosters.
fix: Build noGames start-out only from returning seasons, or condition on being on a roster at the start.

title: playRate clamps every forecast's games to [41, 79.5] of 82: low-availability players get up to 10x their forecast games
claim: playRate() computes its prior as min(.97, max(.5, forecast.games/82)). That clamp was copied from the backtest. There the prior is the raw previous-season games count, and the clamp works as a crude regression to the mean. In production forecast.games is already a fitted forecast (projection-model regression/chain, or ESPN's projection). So every player forecast under 41 games is lifted to 41/82, and that share drives expectedPoints() over the whole season through chainCurve. It changes transfer gains, bestPackage, marketAlerts, injuredTargets and team forecasts.
evidence: Held-out 2025/26 run of the projection model (scratch e11.py: pm.Veteran fitted on targets up to 2024/25, unconditional with_games, 484 test players). Players predicted under 41 games (106): mean predicted 29.0, actual 31.2, clamped 41.0. Games MAE 17.7 raw vs 23.1 clamped; season-FP MAE 139.0 vs 182.9. Predicted under 30 (52): actual 20.8, predicted 21.3, clamped 41.0; FP MAE 106.8 vs 201.7. All players: games MAE 17.1 vs 18.2, FP MAE 187 vs 197. Live (clamp.mjs on live-sports-current.json, empty injury map): 60 of 480 market players have forecast.games < 41, and every one gets 40.1 expected season games (Khalifa Diop 17.1->40.0, Blake Hinson 23.7->40.1, Charles Bassey 29.5->40.1, Dereck Lively II 31.3->40.1, Moses Moody 12->40.1). Median +108 FP per player per season, maximum +416, +6,384 FP in total. The clamp does help with a raw previous-season prior: backtest n=0 MAE 0.2113 clamped vs 0.2173 raw (e10.py). That is why it fits the calibration but not the model forecast.
impact: 12.5% of the market (fringe, injury-prone and rookie-depth players) is overvalued by about 100-400 FP over the season horizon, against a verdict threshold of 15 FP. Season-protected packages and the injured-target list can recommend players the model itself expects to play 15-30 games.
fix: In playRate use prior = clamp(forecast.games/82, 0.01, 0.99) (keep .85 only when games is missing). Keep the [.5,.97] clamp only inside inseason_calibration.py, where the prior is the raw previous season. Then re-run the availability grid with a model-quality prior (k=15-20 was optimal for both). Regression test: a player with forecast.games=20 and no games played must get expectedPoints(...season).games close to 20*80/82.

title: Known injuries are counted twice: forecast games that already exclude an absence are re-applied as the post-return share after the ESPN report removes the same games
claim: expectedPoints sets each future game's chance to injuryFactor (0 until returnDate) times chainCurve(h, share), where share = playRate = forecast.games/82 (clamped). For ESPN-covered players forecast.games is ESPN's projection, and for long injuries ESPN plainly prices the absence in. For healthyNow=false model players it is the unconditional chain mean, which already includes a generic season-start absence. The report then zeroes the absence a second time, and the reduced season share is applied again to the games after the player returns. With the [.5,.97] clamp the error can go either way.
evidence: dbl.mjs (live data, today 2026-10-20, season horizon). Jimmy Butler: ESPN 39 games, out until 2027-01-02, 48 club games after return; app 25.4 games (share 0.50); -13.6 games, -282 FP. Shaedon Sharpe: ESPN 27, out until 2027-03-02 (21 club games after); app 12.2; -14.8 games, -194 FP. Kristaps Porzingis: ESPN 59, back 2026-12-01 (60 games after); app 44.0; -15.0 games, -248 FP. Julian Strawther: 66 -> 51.3. Mouhamed Gueye: 70 -> 55.9. Nic Claxton: 69 -> 61.6. Moses Moody: ESPN 12, back 12-01; the clamp lifts share to 0.5, so app 31.0 (+19 games, +209 FP). Donte DiVincenzo: ESPN 4, app 3.9 (right only because clamp and double count cancel). Totals like 39 for Butler or 4 for DiVincenzo are impossible as healthy shares, so ESPN has priced the injuries in. I could not check, player by player, whether ESPN's shorter-injury projections price the absence.
impact: Long-term injured stars, the target of injuredTargets ('buy before the price reacts') and of the 'season investment' verdict, are undervalued by about 100-300 FP over the season. Some injured fringe players are overvalued through the clamp. That flips acquisition() and verdicts whose threshold is 15 FP.
fix: Store a healthy (conditional) availability share in the forecast: the chain's healthy_mean for model players, and for ESPN players its implied post-return share min(.97, games / club games after the reported return). When a report with returnDate is applied, give playRate that healthy share for the post-return games. Measure on 2026/27 by comparing predicted and actual games after return for players listed Out at forecast time.

title: In-season FP/game estimate runs 0.3-0.48 FP/game low after 5+ games; the MAE-only calibration hides it (early-season games are about 1 FP below the season level)
claim: The calibration selects and reports only MAE, which targets the conditional median. Expected points, gains and team forecasts are sums, so they need a mean-unbiased per-game rate. Within each player, the first ~10 played games run about 1.0 FP and 1.2-1.35 minutes below his season mean, and October below every later month. Pooling those games with the prior pulls the rest-of-season estimate down. The JSON reports no bias at all.
evidence: e4.py, held-out 2024/25->2025/26, production weights (20,5,20). Bias by checkpoint: n0 +0.14, n5 -0.30, n8 -0.35, n12 -0.33, n16 -0.41, n20 -0.32, n30 -0.48, n40 -0.45 (overall -0.254). The same pattern holds with a better Marcel prior (+0.51 at n0 -> -0.05 at n5, so the update shifts by about -0.55). e5.py, players with >=50 games: FP minus own season mean in games 1-10 = -1.05 / -1.01 / -0.87 and minutes -1.17 / -1.20 / -1.12 (2023/24, 24/25, 25/26); October -1.56 / -1.46 / -1.29 FP. MSE-optimal weights (30,5,12) leave bias at -0.232. e15.py: subtracting game-index offsets estimated on the previous season (no leakage) before pooling gives bias +0.027 overall and -0.012 for n>=5, RMSE 2.8986 -> 2.8891, MAE 2.2833 -> 2.2853 (gain CI [-0.028, 0.023]).
impact: A player with 5-30 games played is valued about 0.35-0.45 FP/game below one with none (returning injured, new signings). Over about 50 remaining games that is 18-23 FP, more than transferVerdict's 15 FP threshold. Team season forecasts run about -0.37 x 10 players x ~60 games = about -220 FP per team. That is place-neutral, but the shown totals are biased.
fix: Report mean bias and RMSE next to MAE in data/inseason-calibration.json, and choose the weights on a loss that matches the use (squared error, or MAE plus a bias check). Add a per-game-index offset, estimated on the previous complete season (as in e15.py), to observed FP and minutes in perGame, or a per-checkpoint mean correction. Acceptance: held-out |bias| < 0.1 at every checkpoint with MAE no worse.

title: Rate x minutes treats the fixed participation bonus (+2 at 10+ min, else +1) as if it scaled with minutes; a participation-aware split and role-change detection beat the shipped rule
claim: split() and perGame() predict FP = (FP per minute incl. participation) x expected minutes. The participation term is a step function of minutes, not proportional to them, so a 15 -> 25 minute role change scales a ~1.6 FP bonus to ~2.7 (and the reverse). Separately, genuine minute increases are under-predicted. Players whose first n>=5 games are 6+ minutes above the prior get rest-of-season predictions 1.51 FP/game too low, against -0.37 for all players.
evidence: e2.py (held-out 2025/26). Participation-aware split: counting points per minute shrunk as before, plus expected participation from the recency-weighted 10-minute indicator. Fit-optimal (20,3,20): MAE 2.2833 -> 2.2691, player-clustered 95% gain vs production [0.0019, 0.0266]. Minutes-up subset (207 cases / 53 players): MAE 2.2055 -> 2.0953, bias -1.512 -> -1.321. e16.py adaptive rule (last-5 mean minutes 8+ from the prior -> minuteGames 3, half-life 5): MAE 2.2833 -> 2.2733, gain CI [0.0038, 0.0165]; minutes-up subset MAE 2.205 -> 2.127. Winsorising short games gave nothing (e9.py, CI [-0.005, 0.007]).
impact: Small on average (0.01-0.02 FP/game MAE). Larger for role changers, the players most likely to be transfer targets, where error drops by about 0.1 FP/game.
fix: In inseason_calibration.py, add split_part (from e2.py) and the adaptive minutes branch to the grid, keep them only if the held-out gain CI stays above 0, and mirror them in perGame. The forecast already has components.participation and sources.model.perMinute to separate counting rate from participation. Add a JS<->Python golden test.

title: User-facing method text and docs state stale numbers: 'prior weight 10 games', 'official Sports.ru points', old held-out MAE
claim: The Transfers method text says the per-game forecast moves toward actual points 'вес прогноза — 10 матчей'. That is the fallback rule only. The real estimator weighs 20 (established) or 30 (newcomer) prior games on points per minute, plus 5 or 2 games on minutes with half-lives of 20 and 5. The overview, Teams and KPI text call the points 'официальные (фэнтези-)очки Sports.ru'. Since 20.10 they are FBL points (Sports.ru minus the team result bonus, per collect_sports_current.fbl_points), not Sports.ru's official number. ACCEPTANCE.md:97 still gives held-out MAE '2.37 -> 2.30' and '2.70 -> 2.55', where the shipped JSON has 2.3444 -> 2.2833 and 2.8367 -> 2.6762.
evidence: grep: season-ui.js:640 'вес прогноза — 10 матчей'; season-ui.js:639 'Очки — официальные фэнтези-очки Sports.ru'; :642 and :415 'Факт — официальные очки Sports.ru за период'. data/inseason-calibration.json holdout: established 2.3444/2.2833, newcomer 2.8367/2.6762. The ACCEPTANCE numbers match the pre-#84 JSON (git show 73328bf: 2.3675/2.3016, 2.7049/2.5549).
impact: Users read a false description of how fast estimates react, and believe the standings figure is Sports.ru's own number (it differs by ±2-3 per game).
fix: Rewrite METHOD.transfers to describe the calibrated rule, with numbers taken from CALIBRATION at runtime. Replace 'официальные очки Sports.ru' with 'очки FBL (формула Sports.ru без бонуса за результат)'. Update ACCEPTANCE.md:97, ideally generated from the JSON.

title: Newcomer rateGames=30 is not a stable parameter, and 2023/24 truncated minutes bias the fit pair's prior
claim: The 2023/24 logs carry truncated integer minutes (TRUNCATED_INTEGER_MINUTES, mean team minutes 236.1 vs 241.3 in later seasons). The fit pair's prior minutes are therefore about 2.2% low and its prior rate about 2.2% high, which fakes a minutes rise between prior and observed games. Adding the expected +0.5 minute flips the newcomer choice from 30 to 20 rate games with no significant test difference. The 20.10 changelog presents 'newcomers now weigh 30 games of prior' as an effect of removing the bonus, but that difference is noise.
evidence: e13.py: shipped grid -> established (20,5,20), newcomer (30,2,5). With 2023/24 minutes +0.5 -> established (20,5,20), newcomer (20,2,5). Test newcomer MAE 2.6762 (30) vs 2.6691 (20). normalize_minutes reports 2023-24 TRUNCATED_INTEGER_MINUTES.
impact: Small (<0.01 FP/game), but the stated parameter and its narrative are not supported.
fix: De-truncate 2023/24 minutes (+0.5 per row, or rescale to 240 per team game) in load(). Report a bootstrap selection frequency or flat-optimum range for each parameter instead of a single argmin.

title: season_accuracy.py validates a model whose forecasts are always overwritten; its holdout numbers describe nothing users see
claim: build_forecasts.py fits SeasonModel (k-NN deltas plus split-conformal) and writes version-2 forecasts. projection_model.py (v4) and complete_forecasts.py (v3) then replace every one of them. The SeasonModel holdout (selectedModelSeasonMAE 286, empirical80RangeCoverage 0.80) survives only in forecast-audit.json / database.forecastAudit. CI checks only that holdout.players > 100, and no UI reads it.
evidence: default-draft.json forecast versions: v4 871 (CAREER_MODEL 500, ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED 313, DRAFT_PICK_MODEL 40, UNDRAFTED 18), v3 3, v2 0. grep: forecastAudit is referenced only by complete_forecasts.py, build_forecasts.py and verify-build.js, never in src/. projection_model.apply reads only the ESPN_INDIVIDUAL meanPerGame/games from the v2 stage, not SeasonModel's point_parts or interval.
impact: Readers of forecast-audit.json may take its 0.80 coverage and MAE as the accuracy of the shown forecasts. Every build spends CPU on an O(n^2) leave-player-out search that has no effect.
fix: Remove the SeasonModel stage, or label forecastAudit.holdout 'legacy fallback, not used'. Point the build check at projectionModelAudit.holdout instead.

title: Players without forecast minutes fall back to a 10-game simple shrink and never use the calibrated newcomer rule
claim: withMarket() priors (SPORTS_PRICE_PRIOR) carry no minutes, so perGame takes the PRIOR_GAMES=10 fallback. The newcomer() test for SPORTS_PRICE_PRIOR is therefore unreachable. For group-prior newcomers the MAE-optimal simple shrink is 3 games, not 10. For established players 10 is the right fallback.
evidence: e14.py: best simple k on the fit pair, established 10 (test 2.3444), newcomers 3 (test 2.8212 vs 2.8367 at k=10). market.mjs: 2 market-only players now (Alex Antetokounmpo, Tamar Bates; prior 7.10, minutes undefined). After 5 games of 30 FP at 34 min, fallback 14.73 vs 13.77 on the newcomer path with a 20-minute prior.
impact: Only 2 players today, but every new market entrant during the season goes through this path.
fix: Give market priors a minutes value (median forecast.minutes of the same-price players) so the calibrated newcomer branch applies, or use k=3 in the fallback when newcomer(p).

title: Season horizon counts only the 80 published club games while forecasts are per 82
claim: Every Sports.ru club calendar lists 80 games (the 2 NBA Cup games are added in December). chainCurve scales the share over 82 games, but expectedPoints sums only the 80 calendar games. Until December every season-horizon expectation is about 2.4% short of forecast.games x meanPerGame.
evidence: live-sports-current.json: 30 clubs x 80 games (Counter({80: 30})), last date 2027-04-12 MSK.
impact: Uniform about -2 games per player (about -300 FP per team season). Places are unchanged, but the shown season forecasts and per-period totals on the Teams tab are understated.
fix: Until the calendar reaches 82, add (82 - calendar length) x share pseudo-games at the end of the season horizon, or label the season total as covering published games only.

title: No test pins the JS estimator to the Python calibration estimator
claim: The JS perGame and Python split agree today (my harness), but no test would catch drift: a change in one language would silently invalidate the published calibration. The JS test 'calibrated update beats the old rule' only re-reads numbers from the JSON.
evidence: gen_cases.py + cmp.mjs: 300 random cases (1-40 games, both cohorts, m:ss minutes), max |js - py| = 2.8e-14.
impact: Guards the claim that production uses the fitted rule.
fix: Commit a small golden fixture (prior, obs, expected value from Python split) and assert perGame matches within 1e-9 in tests/season.test.js.

title: Exact completion solver lets a 'forced' rookie become a third player of a club that is already full: illegal witness, too-low minimum cost, and false 'possible'
claim: When the cheapest roster found by flowSelect has no rookie, clubCompletion forces each rookie in turn by adding it to the fixed set (line 116). In flowSelect the source->club capacity is Math.max(CLUB_LIMIT, held), where held counts every fixed player of that club, and now that includes the forced rookie (line 131). So if the team already has 2 players from club X, forcing a rookie from X sets held=3 and the capacity rises to 3. The solver then returns a roster with three X players. It reports possible:true, a minimumCost that is too low, and a playerIds witness that breaks the club rule. The max(...,held) was meant to tolerate legacy fixed picks, but it switches the club rule off for the forced rookie. The test suite cannot catch this because its brute-force tests fix at most one player (fixed=seed%2?[players[0].id]:[]), and the bug needs at least two fixed players from the rookie's club. So the ACCEPTANCE claim that '3,000 random brute-force cases ... agree exactly' is not true for the shipped code.
evidence: Independent oracle: DFS over all 10-man rosters, with Hall-condition position check, club<=2, rookie>=1 and cap (scratchpad/audit/draft-completion-solver/fuzz2.mjs). Current code: 6 mismatches in 2,116 checks (seed 7), 4 in 1,512 (fuzz3, two same-club players fixed) and 3 in 936 (fuzz4). Patched copy (completion-patched.mjs skips a forced rookie whose club already holds CLUB_LIMIT fixed players): 0 mismatches in about 7,000 checks across the same generators (ties, cap exactly at the minimum and minimum-1, missing prices, OFF mode, multi-position players, null clubs, rookies all at one club). Real data (realdraft2.mjs replays the real 80 picks on public/data/default-draft.json, 25,554 completion checks): 168 illegal witnesses, 176 cost differences, all for team 4 at picks 61-69 and all 100 too low. Example (team4.mjs) after 62 picks: ORIG minimumCost 18900 / remaining 2000 with witness '...Tyrese Haliburton(PG,Индиана), Ivica Zubac(C,Индиана), ..., Braden Smith(PG,Индиана,1000,R)' (3 Indiana players); FIX 19000 / 2100 with Christian Anderson (Шарлотт,1100,R). Feasibility flip (flip.mjs, cap 19000, two IND SF fixed, the only cheap rookie is an IND PG): ORIGINAL 'true 17600' vs PATCHED 'false 19100 ... превышает лимит 19000'.
impact: The status line 'добор от X' (main.js:479), the pick gate (main.js:92,146 via pickCompletion), rookie-watch/rookies and the bots in the plan/availability simulations all trust a witness that can be illegal. In the real draft this only understated team 4's minimum completion budget by 100 for 8 states, with no feasibility flip. In tighter states (budget or rookie scarcity) the gate approves a pick that leaves no legal completion: the team gets stuck at its 10th pick, where pick() refuses the club-violating rookie. Training drafts, simulations and any future draft are affected.
fix: In clubCompletion, before forcing a rookie, count the fixed players per club and skip any rookie whose club already holds CLUB_LIMIT fixed players: `const club=clubOf(rookie);if(club!==null&&candidates.filter(p=>fixed.has(p.id)&&clubOf(p)===club).length>=CLUB_LIMIT)continue;`. Better still, pass the club capacity computed from the original fixed set into flowSelect instead of Math.max(CLUB_LIMIT,held). Add a regression test (two fixed players of club X; the only affordable rookie is from X; expect possible:false or the dearer legal minimum). Extend the brute-force tests to fix 2-4 players with forced same-club pairs. Correct ACCEPTANCE.md:127. Measure with the fuzz scripts: mismatches should be 0.

title: Draft-state player snapshots never refresh: the Season tab, team forecasts and post-draft standings use draft-day forecasts (including the removed team-result bonus) for every drafted player
claim: installDatabase rebuilds each picked player as {...selectedSnapshot, price/priceStatus/positions from the new DB}. forecast, projectedFP, isRookie, sportsClub, injuries, forecast.games and forecast.availability.hazards all stay as they were at the moment of the pick, through every later database update. compactDraft saves these snapshots and restoreBudgetDraft/installDatabase restore them, so they persist indefinitely. main.js render() passes state.players to setSeasonPlayers, so the Season tab (perGame prior = forecast.meanPerGame, playRate prior = forecast.games, rules check isRookie) runs on these frozen records for every drafted player. Free agents get the current database. The forecast pipeline was rebuilt several times after the 18.10 draft: career model #39 (19.10), team-bonus model #43, availability Markov chain #46, ESPN games #61, and the team-result bonus removed in #84 (20.10). A device that recorded the draft on 18.10 therefore compares drafted players under the draft-day model with free agents under the current one. In training mode, state.players is the training draft, so the season numbers also depend on which draft mode is open. The status line still says 'База … обновлена <new date>'.
evidence: scratchpad/audit/draft-completion-solver/snapshot.mjs: installed the deployed DB, recorded the 80 real picks, saved with compactDraft, restored with restoreBudgetDraft, then installed a 'new' DB with forecast.scoringBreakdown.teamResult removed (what #84 does). Output: 'picked players with forecast != new DB: 80 of 80, max |d| 1.03, >0.5: 39'; 'SGA state 30.21 new DB 29.19, databaseVersion 2026-10-21T00:00:00Z'. The team-result component of the 80 drafted players ranges from -0.95 (Sabonis) to +1.03 FP/game (SGA, Holmgren, J. Williams, Hartenstein); 39/80 have |component| > 0.5. ACCEPTANCE.md:225 confirms the #84 forecasts move by -1.0 to +1.0 per game.
impact: Every swap or package suggestion that sells a drafted player compares a stale prior (up to +/-1 FP/game from the bonus alone, plus all model changes since 18.10) with a fresh one for the buy candidate. That is about 3-4 FP over a 7-day horizon and about 70 FP over a season per affected player, and the bias decays only slowly as games arrive (prior weight 10-30 games). Team forecasts on the Teams tab and post-draft standings carry the same bias for all 8 teams. The rookie flags in the device's rules check are also frozen. If the owner's device holds the recorded LIVE draft, these are materially wrong numbers shown to the user.
fix: Keep the draft-time snapshot only where the draft analysis needs it (for example p.draftSnapshot) and refresh forecast, projectedFP, isRookie, injuries, availability and club from the new database in installDatabase. At minimum, feed the Season tab from the database catalog rather than the draft state: setSeasonPlayers(database?.players ?? state.players), with the snapshot overlay used only in the draft tab. Measure by re-running snapshot.mjs: 0 of 80 players should differ from the new DB.

title: Re-picking an earlier pick can silently leave a team with no legal completion (gate ignores the team's later kept picks)
claim: chooseReplacement checks pickCompletion(replaceBase,p.id) against the draft cut at the replaced index, so the team's own later picks are not fixed. replacePick then replays the later picks with pick(), which checks only the hard rules (positions, clubs, per-pick cap, rookie at the 10th) and not completion feasibility. When every later pick replays, nothing is dropped, no confirm appears and the toast reports success. But the team's committed roster can now need more than the cap (or have no rookie slot left), so its next pick has no legal player.
evidence: scratchpad/audit/draft-completion-solver/replace.mjs on the real draft after 72 picks: 11 UI-approved replacements with 'nothing dropped' leave a team impossible. Examples: 'pick #41 team 0: Kon Knueppel -> Jimmy Butler III (2300): nothing dropped, but Минимальный бюджет полного состава 20100.00 превышает лимит 20000'; 'pick #37 team 4: Franz Wagner -> Kawhi Leonard (2400): ... 20400.00 ...'.
impact: A correction made through 'Перевыбрать' during a live or training draft can strand a team. Its next pick shows every card disabled (and for a rival in LIVE mode the real pick cannot be recorded, see the next finding), so the user has to undo picks without having been warned. The real draft is finished, so the current impact is limited to training and future drafts.
fix: After replacePick, run completionPlan(result.state, team) for the replaced team (and for any team whose kept picks were replayed) and refuse or confirm when it fails. Alternatively, gate the replacement with the team's later kept picks treated as fixed. Add a test using the pick #41 Knueppel->Butler case.

title: The LIVE-mode override for recording a rival's real pick is dead code; ACCEPTANCE claims it works
claim: choose() would let a rival's pick that the app thinks leaves no completion be recorded after confirm() in LIVE mode. But the only path into choose() for a rival is the card button, and cardAction disables that button whenever pickCompletion(...).possible===false. So the confirm branch is unreachable. ACCEPTANCE.md:132 says 'in live mode a rival's real pick that the app thinks leaves no completion can still be recorded after confirmation', which is false. The same logic was already present before the redesign (d9e7b7c^ line 118).
evidence: grep shows choose( is called only from main.js:89 (replacement), 103 (plan buttons, own team only) and 145 (card button). main.js:146-149: `const plan=pickCompletion(target(),p.id);if(plan.possible===false)reason=plan.reason; ... if(reason){b.disabled=true;...}`. There are no keyboard handlers (grep keydown/Enter: none) and no test covers the override.
impact: If the app's data disagrees with Sports.ru (prices, rookie flags, positions), or after a bad replacement (previous finding), a real rival pick cannot be entered. The LIVE draft then cannot advance, or the user records a different player and corrupts the record. The real 2026 draft replays cleanly (all 80 picks pass pickCompletion), so the effect is latent.
fix: In cardAction, for a rival pick in LIVE mode, keep the button enabled when only the completion check fails and show the reason as a warning; keep it disabled for hard pick() errors. Or remove the dead branch and correct ACCEPTANCE.md:132.

title: completionPlan accepts fixed sets that already break the club rule; rookiesLeftAfter overcounts usable rookies
claim: completionPlan never checks that the fixed picks themselves satisfy the club rule. flowSelect widens each club's capacity to the held count, and the fast path's clubAwareGreedy keeps all fixed players. simulation.js rookiesLeftAfter appends each rookie as an unvalidated pick ({team,playerId}) and asks completionPlan, so a rookie from a club where the team already has 2 players is counted as usable. The bots' rookie-scarcity guard (needsRookie && tight && rookiesLeftAfter <= teamsNeedingRookie) is therefore too optimistic.
evidence: scratchpad/audit/draft-completion-solver/rookiesleft.mjs: team with two IND SF fixed plus an IND rookie appended as a pick -> 'completion with 3rd IND player as fixed pick: true 10'. pick() would refuse that rookie (clubsFit).
impact: Bots in training mode and in the plan's availability simulations may skip a needed rookie reservation. In 40 bot drafts on the real database no run failed, so the effect is small. The same root cause as the forced-rookie bypass.
fix: At the top of completionPlan, return {possible:false, reason:'клубный лимит'} when !clubsFit(fixedPlayers). In rookiesLeftAfter, validate the hypothetical pick with pick() (try/catch) before calling completionPlan.

title: White rule is enforced in the draft plan MILP but not in the pick gate, the completion solver or the bots
claim: planRoster adds white>=1 when the league list exists ('the draft plan keeps one in the ten' is true there). completionPlan/pickCompletion and pick() ignore the white rule, though they enforce the rookie rule. So the 'Выбрать' buttons, the 'добор от' line and the bots allow a final roster with no white-list player, and the plan then answers 'Нет допустимого плана' with no reason. The exchange-argument pruning key (positions|club|rookie) also leaves out the white flag, so adding white later without changing the key would break exactness.
evidence: grep: white appears only in plan.js/main.js (plan worker), season*.js and rules.js, never in engine.js or completion.js. Checking DRAFT_PICKS against data/fbl-league.json white (100 ids): team 7's draft roster has 0 white players, teams 2, 5 and 6 have exactly 1.
impact: For practice and future drafts, own-team picks can break the white rule without warning, and the plan and the gate disagree. Opponent simulations generate rosters the league would flag. For the 18.10 draft there was no list yet, so there is no retroactive harm.
fix: Pass the WHITE list into completionPlan/pickCompletion. Add the white flag to the pruning group key. Enforce it like the rookie rule: if the base lacks white, force each white candidate in turn; if it lacks both, force a player who is both or rookie+white pairs, still polynomial after pruning. Or reuse the plan's MILP for the gate. Make pick() refuse a 10th pick that leaves no white player when a list is configured.

title: Shipped database JSON carries stale limitation texts ('no unconfirmed NBA club limit is imposed', 'positions mapped from ESPN', 'No official prices')
claim: forecastAudit.limitations says no NBA club limit is imposed, but the 2-per-club rule is enforced since 19.10 (league-rules nbaClubLimit=2). The top-level limitations say positions come from ESPN and there are no official prices, while positionAuthority is Sports.ru and 480 prices are VERIFIED Sports.ru prices.
evidence: node: d.limitations -> ['Positions are mapped from ESPN basketball positions, not verified Yahoo eligibility.', ..., 'No official prices, result bonuses, calibrated injury probability or validated season forecast.']; build_forecasts.py:150 '...no unconfirmed NBA club limit is imposed.'; d.positionAuthority='Sports.ru', 480 VERIFIED prices.
impact: Not rendered in the UI today (grep: no src reads limitations or forecastAudit), but it is published and contradicts the rules. Anyone reading the audit JSON gets false provenance.
fix: Update or remove these strings in build_forecasts.py and build_default_database.py so they match data/league-rules.json and the price and position audits.

title: 'Шанс дожить' survival odds have no skill on the real 2026 FBL draft. They are overconfident, and the opponent models give 31% of real picks zero probability
location: src/plan.js:15-28, src/plan.js:32-63, src/simulation.js:47-83, src/main.js:305, src/main.js:314, src/main.js:321, src/main.js:328
claim: The plan's survival-to-next-pick probabilities come from 50 simulated drafts: 25 runs with forecast bots (top-8 pool, 3 styles) and 25 with ADP plus noise sd 1.5+0.2*ADP. The UI shows them as 'Шанс дожить', 'Шанс' and 'доживёт до #N: X%', and uses them as hard 80% deadlines. Replayed at each of our 9 real picks (1..65) of the actual 18.10 draft, they predict which players survive no better than a constant. 22 of the 70 real opponent picks were impossible under both opponent models. Real GMs choose far more dispersedly than either model: the median ADP rank of the chosen player among those available was 13, and only 46% of picks fell in the bot's top-8 value pool. The KM estimate from 50 runs has no smoothing, so 0 losses in 50 runs is shown as 100%.
evidence:
Scripts: scratchpad/audit/draft-sim/t3.mjs (backtest), a3b.py, t5.mjs plus a5.py (likelihood). Fair candidate set = top-30 by value plus top-30 by ADP at each of our picks, n=333, 54 lost.
- Brier score: model 0.1340, constant base rate 0.1359. Log loss: model 0.486, constant 0.443, so the model is worse than a constant.
- Calibration bins (mean predicted vs realised survival): 0.13->0.38, 0.28->0.59, 0.50->0.68, 0.72->0.89, 0.85->0.70, 0.94->0.89, 0.98->0.925, 1.00->0.941.
- Shown as 100%: 6 of 102 lost (Davis at pick 8, Irving, F. Wagner, Lillard, Anunoby, Hart, Zubac, George, Gobert, McDaniels across all players).
- Plan-eligible players (pred>=0.8): realised loss 11.4% vs 4.3% predicted.
- Planned future players in real plans (t9.mjs): 24 of 35 were still there at their planned pick (69%), though each was scored >=80%.
- Opponent picks impossible in 150 single-pick draws from both models: 22 of 70 (picks 8, 27, 31, 32, 34, 35, 37, 38, 39, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 52, 53, 59, 61, 62, 70, 74, 80).
- Simply shrinking the predictions 30% toward the base rate improves Brier to 0.1233 and log loss to 0.401.
impact: Every draft-plan probability the GM saw: the now-or-wait decision, the 80% deadline that admits or excludes players, and the mandatory-rookie timing. Boozer was planned for pick 33 at 88-94% survival and went at 32, then four more rookies went by pick 42. The draft is over, so this now affects training mode and the next draft. The survival estimates are the main input to the plan.
fix: 1) Replace the two ad-hoc opponent models with a fitted discrete-choice model, P(j) proportional to exp(b1*ADP-rank + b2*our-value-rank + b3*rookie*round + b4*position-need). Fit it by maximum likelihood on the 70 observed FBL opponent picks, with cross-validation across rounds, and refit after each future draft. 2) Smooth the KM hazards with a Beta prior (for example Jeffreys) and/or isotonic recalibration on backtests, so 0 losses in 50 runs is never shown as 100%. 3) Add this backtest (Brier/log loss vs a constant) as a build check. Measure the gain as Brier/log loss on held-out rounds.

title: The draft objective penalises downside spread, but for P(first) variance is worth +0.5 to +1.4 FP of mean per FP of team sd for every FBL team
location: src/valuation.js:32-37, src/plan.js:66, src/plan.js:71-106, src/simulation.js:37-38, src/main.js:296, src/main.js:328
claim: The plan's MILP maximises sum of riskAdjustedValue*82 = slotSeason - 0.14*(meanSeason - seasonFloor), the 'balanced' style. That is a risk-averse utility on our total. FBL ranks 8 teams by total points, so the natural objectives are P(1st), expected place or expected prize. Under P(1st) adding variance raises our chances. In a symmetric 8-team league, 1 FP of team sd is worth 0.98 FP of mean. On the real post-draft standings it is worth +0.48 FP for the favourite (us) up to +1.43 FP for the weakest team. Under expected place the value is about 0 at draft time (symmetric) and -0.36 only for the favourite. No rank-based objective supports a fixed downside penalty for all teams. The penalty is also measured on own points (mean - floor), while the value is the slot (own + replacement). Most of the own downside is absences, which the slot concept says transfers cover, so injury-prone low-FP/game players are penalised for risk the slot value already removed.
evidence:
Normal approximation (scratch python):
- Symmetric league: dP1/dmu = 1.369e-4, dP1/dsd = 1.346e-4.
- Post-draft (means 15244/14415/14462/15123/13742/13762/13822/13897, sds about 1281-1484): value of 1 FP of team sd = 0.481, 0.963, 0.954, 0.551, 1.432, 1.415, 1.356, 1.312.
Real sampler, common random numbers, 100k runs (t18.mjs):
- Team 1: P1 28.06% -> 29.33% with an extra zero-mean sd-600 player-sized noise, vs 30.23% with +100 FP of mean.
- Team 5: 4.41% -> 5.64% with the noise vs 5.09% with +100 FP.
- So a player with sd 600 (mean-floor 769) is worth +59 to +180 FP relative to a riskless one, while valuation.js charges him -108 FP: a 170-290 FP swing per volatile player.
Plan replay at 10 real picks with STYLE_DOWNSIDE 0.14 / 0 / -0.14 (t7.mjs): the now-pick is identical for balanced and neutral (10/10), but changes at 3/10 picks under a variance-seeking proxy (25 Leonard vs Murray, 33 Leonard vs Giddey, 57 Porter Jr. vs Daniels). The planned future rosters differ by 3-5 players.
impact: All draft advice: the plan's 'лучший состав', the 'ФО*' column, the alternatives' deltas, the bots, and the Telegram/card 'value per 1000' pros/cons via insights.js. It is systematically biased toward low-variance players in a contest that rewards variance. The UI says the plan is an 'exact optimisation of season forecasts', not of a preference.
fix: Make the objective explicit and derive it. Option 1: maximise P(1st), or expected prize if payouts exist, by sample-average approximation: for each top-K now-candidate, run paired rollouts (calibrated opponents, our team re-planned by the MILP) followed by the standings Monte Carlo of simulation.js, using common random numbers and sequential halving or UCB to spend runs on close candidates. Option 2 (cheap): use risk-neutral slotSeason as the default and add an optional variance term lambda*Var_slot with lambda set from dP1/dsd of the current standings (the sign is positive for all 8 teams now). Measure in simulation: the P(1st) of the policy vs the current one over 1000 paired simulated drafts plus seasons.

title: Kaplan-Meier censoring is informative through the bot/ADP mixture: survival of the player our simulated team takes most often is overstated by 8-17 pp
claim: Our own simulated pick censors a player only in the bot half of the runs. The ADP-run 'us' rarely takes forecast favourites. The surviving at-risk set for the next interval is therefore dominated by ADP runs, where nobody else takes him either. The pooled hazard then mixes the two models with weights set by our own choices instead of the intended 50/50. A per-model (stratified) estimate, or a counterfactual run where our team never takes X, gives much lower survival. The other players are unaffected, so the bookkeeping itself is right.
evidence:
Counterfactual check (t4.mjs; our team forbidden from taking X; same seeds; 50 runs):
- State after 8 real picks: Jalen Duren KM 0.69/0.55 vs counterfactual 0.52/0.40 at picks 17/25.
- State after 24 picks: Jamal Murray 0.42/0.12 vs 0.34/0.10.
- The other 38 players match within +-0.04.
Decomposition for Duren (t14.mjs):
- Bot runs: our bot took him in 14 of 25; in the other 11 opponents took him every time (hazard 11/11).
- ADP runs: at risk 25, lost 0.
- Pooled hazard 11/36 = 0.31 (survival 0.69) vs equal-weight stratified hazard 0.50 (survival 0.50; counterfactual 0.52).
impact: This is the take-now-or-wait candidate, where the decision matters most. A 0.69 vs 0.52 error can move a player across the 80% deadline and change the plan's now-pick. In the two states tested both values fell below 0.8, so the decision there was the same.
fix: Estimate hazards separately for each opponent model and average the survival curves with the intended weights. Better: for the top ~15 plan candidates, run counterfactual simulations in which our team never takes X; this costs about 15x50 partial drafts to the next two picks. Keep the neighbour pooling only for the remaining players.

title: The plan's headline value assumes every planned player survives; the joint survival of the displayed plan is only 30-51%
claim: planRoster turns each player's survival into a hard deadline (survival >= 0.8, otherwise excluded). It then reports value = the sum over the planned roster as if every planned player will be there. The chip next to 'Твой пик: бери сейчас' shows this deterministic best case. Survival above the threshold is ignored (0.81 and 1.00 count the same) and the risk of losing several planned players is never priced. The realised value of following the plan with re-planning is lower and differs by candidate. A candidate whose plan leans on many 0.8-0.85 players looks as good as one with safe follow-ups.
evidence:
t9.mjs, real draft states:
- Product of the plan's survival odds: pick 1 30% (plan 14339 FP), pick 9 35%, pick 17 33%, pick 25 51%, pick 33 50%.
- In the real draft, 2-4 planned players per plan were gone before their planned pick. At 17: Boozer (planned 33, gone at 32), F. Wagner (planned 49, gone at 37), Lillard (planned 57, gone at 39), Podziemski (planned 65, gone at 60).
impact: The GM sees an optimistic total and the 'Если взять другого' deltas. Both overstate how reliable a plan is, especially when it depends on late rookies (the rookie constraint).
fix: Report and compare candidates by expected value under the simulated futures. For each now-candidate, solve the deadline-free completion per scenario (scenario-specific availability) and average: a two-stage stochastic programme or sample-average approximation. Or at least use expected value = sum of v_i*s_i + (1-s_i)*best fallback. Show the plan's joint survival. Measure by replaying the plan policy against simulated (or real) drafts and comparing the realised roster value with the displayed value.

title: Post-draft standings and roster totals use pick-time forecast snapshots, so the removed team-result bonus and older models persist after the database is refreshed
claim: installDatabase keeps each picked player's snapshot ({...selected, plus price/positions only}) and copies forecasts from the old snapshot. This is by design ('Picked players retain the exact roster/projection snapshot used when selected'). For a completed real draft this means the 'Прогноз сезона и составы' standings (5000-run P(first), the 8-of-10 ranges) and the 'Прогноз X ФО' chip of 'Мой состав' are computed from forecasts frozen when each pick was recorded (18.10). Later model changes never reach these picks: slot/transfer values, the team-result bonus removal of 20.10, injury updates. The currently deployed DB (built 2026-10-20T12:18Z) still contains the bonus inside meanPerGame (Jokic: components teamResult +0.477/game). Rebuilt databases will not fix the snapshots on devices that already recorded the draft.
evidence:
t10.mjs: picked snapshot meanSeason 2649 vs refreshed DB 2549 for Jokic stays 2649 after installDatabase(compactDraft(saved), db). Team-1 standings mean 15602 (snapshot) vs 15231 (fresh).
t11.mjs: team-result bonus inside the deployed meanSeason per FBL team = [84, 64, 226, 92, 21, 214, -2, -26]. Removing it moves P1: team 3 12.8% -> 11.0%, team 8 6.4% -> 7.2%, team 7 6.2% -> 6.9%; means drop by up to 226 FP (team 3) and 213 (team 6).
impact: Every device that recorded the real 80 picks before a DB rebuild. The draft-tab standings and roster totals show a bonus that no longer exists in the league formula, plus pre-20.10 model numbers. Errors are about 200 FP per team for teams 3 and 6 and up to 1.8 pp of P(first).
fix: Keep snapshots only for replay and legality: price/positions/rookie at pick time. Read forecasts for the post-draft standings and roster totals from the current database by id, or at least refresh forecast fields for picked players once the draft is complete. Add a test that a completed draft's standings change when the DB forecast changes.

title: The standings Monte Carlo adds the replacement value as a constant, so slot variance is overstated and P(first) is pulled toward parity
claim: scenarioSeasonScore draws the player's own season from his own-points range and then adds forecast.transfer.value, the expected replacement points, unchanged in every scenario. Replacement points are strongly negatively correlated with own points: a low draw is mostly missed games, and those games are what a transfer fills. A slot's spread is therefore much narrower than an own-points spread, and the standings model overstates every team's sd. Because the overstatement is roughly common, it compresses P(first) toward 1/8. (Opposing effect: on held-out data the player ranges cover 74%, not 80%, which alone would widen them by about 14%.)
evidence:
Mean-preserving coupling experiment (t6c.mjs, 20k runs): replacement = transfer.value + cc*replacementPerGame*(E[own]-own)/meanPerGame, with cc = replacedGames/(82-games), clipped at 0, rescaled so its mean equals transfer.value; team means unchanged to within 5 FP.
- Team sd falls from 1281/1484/1433/1363/1341/1350/1392/1392 to 1093/1198/1204/1194/1005/1053/1054/1154 (-12% to -25%).
- P1 changes: team 1 28.0 -> 31.6% (30.3% at half coupling), team 4 24.8 -> 27.5, team 5 4.4 -> 2.8, team 7 5.7 -> 4.0.
- Widening the ranges to match 74% coverage alone: team 1 28.0 -> 26.8.
impact: The live post-draft table ('1-е место', '8 сезонов из 10') and the training season table. P(first) is understated for favourites by about 2-4 pp and overstated for underdogs by about 1-2 pp. The team ranges are mis-sized by about 15-25%.
fix: Draw availability and rate separately: games from the absence chain that forecast.availability already has, the per-game rate from the rate error. Compute replacement points from the drawn missed long-absence games (the same delay rule). Or, minimally, couple replacement to the own draw as above. Then recalibrate the player ranges to the measured held-out coverage. Validate by back-testing team-level coverage on 2025/26 pseudo-rosters.

title: A completed real draft becomes 'illegal' after any later Sports.ru price or position update, which hides the standings ('по 0 сценариям')
claim: installDatabase writes the latest catalog prices and Sports.ru positions onto picked players, then enforceBudget replays every pick under the cap at those current prices. In-season price changes (or a Sports.ru position change) can push a team that drafted legally above 20000. Team 2 spent exactly 20000 at draft prices. The app then marks the real draft as violating Sports.ru rules ('Отмени пики или начни новый драфт'). seasonSensitivitySimulations throws, the post-draft table vanishes, and the note reads 'Прогноз мест по 0 сценариям сезона'. The cap applies to prices at transaction time, so draft legality must be judged at draft prices.
evidence: t13.mjs: real 80-pick draft, next catalog with Doncic +100 -> pricingIssue 'Сохранённый состав не соответствует правилам Sports.ru: Превышен Salary Cap. Отмени пики или начни новый драфт.' seasonSensitivitySimulations throws 'Составы должны соблюдать позиции Sports.ru, rookie и salary cap'. Team costs at current prices: 19800/20000/19900/19900/19900/19800/19700/19500.
impact: This is latent: it triggers when the dated price catalog (2026-10-17) is refreshed for the season. Then the user's recorded draft is falsely declared illegal and the post-draft forecast disappears with a misleading '0 scenarios' message.
fix: Store the pick-time price in each pick record and validate draft legality against it. Validate current-price budgets only in the season module (the bank). In main.js, show an explicit error instead of 'по 0 сценариям' when standings is null.

title: Draft-tool totals mix metrics: the training season table and the '100 драфтов' winners use own points, while the ranges and the draft ranking use slot value
claim: draftSummary.score = sum of meanSeason (own points only). In the training season table the 'Прогноз' column shows that score and sorts by it, while the '8 из 10' range and '1-е место' come from the simulation, which adds about 630-1224 FP of replacement value per team. The forecast shown can sit near the 20th percentile of its own range, and the order can contradict P(first). batchSimulations picks winners by the same own-points score, while players were drafted by slot value. Also, training bots (advanceBots) all use the 'balanced' style with no rookie habit, unlike the style-mix bots the plan's survival model uses.
evidence:
Real draft, 5000 runs (t1.mjs):
- Team 7: base 12558, range 12098-15613, sim mean 13844, P1 6.2%.
- Team 5: base 12603, mean 13743, P1 4.4%. Team 5 is listed above team 7.
- Transfer value per team = [630, 965, 727, 634, 1115, 902, 1224, 791].
impact: Training-mode readers see inconsistent numbers and an order that contradicts the first-place column. The live post-draft table (sorted by sim mean) is not affected.
fix: Use one season metric (slot season = meanSeason + transfer.value) in draftSummary.score, batch winners and the roster chip. Or label the column 'свои очки без замен'. Give advanceBots the same style and habit sampling as simulateDraft.

title: The LCG seeded with consecutive integers gives almost the same first draw, so the batch always simulates our team with the 'balanced' style
claim: randomFromSeed is a raw LCG, and the seed becomes the state directly. Seeds s and s+1 differ in their first output by a/2^32 = 0.000388, and the k-th outputs form a fixed arithmetic lattice across seeds. batchSimulations uses seeds seed..seed+99, and simulateDraft's first draw sets team 0's style. Every one of the 100 '100 драфтов' runs therefore uses the same style for our team: 'balanced' for every UI seed from 1 to 250. The runs are not independent samples over the styles they claim to vary.
evidence: t8.mjs: u1 over seeds 1..100 lies in [0.2365, 0.2748]; team-0 style counts {balanced: 100}; teams 1-7 are about 1/3 each. Box-Muller quality on a single stream is fine: P(z<-1.2816)=0.0997, P(|z|>3)=0.00273, var 1.0005 over 2M draws.
impact: Small: the batch never varies our simulated style; it is cosmetic for the other teams. Correlated streams can also bias any future paired-seed comparisons.
fix: Scramble the seed before use (for example a splitmix32 or murmur3 fmix32 finaliser), or switch to mulberry32/sfc32 seeded through a hash. Add a test that the first draws for seeds 1..100 are roughly uniform.

title: Player range label 'в 8 сезонах из 10' is not supported by the held-out test (74% coverage, 15% above the ceiling)
claim: Every player card says the season lands between the weak and strong season 'в 8 сезонах из 10'. The standings assumption text says the bounds are '10-й и 90-й процентили, откалиброванные на прошлых сезонах'. The model's own held-out audit for 2025/26 measured 74.0% coverage, with 11.0% below the floor and 15.1% above the ceiling. The upper bound is too low, and the published interval is closer to '7 из 10'. (This overlaps the forecast dimension; it is listed because the draft simulator and standings take these bounds as exact quantiles.)
evidence: public/data/projection-model-audit.json holdout: coverage80 0.7397, belowRange 0.1095, aboveRange 0.1508, coverage80Active 0.758. The sampler reproduces the published bounds exactly as quantiles: max |P10/P90 - floor/ceiling| = 19 FP over the 80 rostered players (t17.mjs).
impact: All player cards and the standings ranges and P(first). Upside is under-modelled for every player.
fix: Either recalibrate the tails to the measured held-out rates (conformal per tail on the latest season too), or state the measured coverage in the UI ('около 3 сезонов из 4').
