title: The '95% доверительный интервал' tooltip for first place covers only Monte Carlo error, not model uncertainty that is 3x larger
claim: The Wilson interval on 5000 runs (about +-1.2 pp at 28%) measures sampling error of the model's own frequency. Reasonable model variations (replacement coupling, coverage-corrected ranges, removing the team-result bonus) move team 1's first-place share between 26.8% and 31.6%, well outside the shown 26.5-28.9% interval. A '95% доверительный интервал' label invites reading it as uncertainty about winning. The note under the table correctly says it is not a win probability.
impact: Training-mode season table tooltip only; it gives a false sense of precision.
fix: Rename it 'точность расчёта (Монте-Карло)'. Or show a model-uncertainty band, for example by bootstrapping range calibration and coupling parameters.

title: Draft survival odds ('Шанс дожить') are overconfident against the real 18.10 FBL draft; a calibrated pick model clearly fits better
claim: availabilityProfile mixes 25 forecast-bot futures with 25 ADP-model futures. I backtested its one-step survival (from each of our 9 turns to our next pick) against what actually happened in DRAFT_PICKS. Its probabilities are too extreme in both directions. Neither half fits the GMs' real behaviour. The bots choose only from the top 8 of their own value ranking (simulation.js:63-64), yet 30 of the 80 real picks were outside the top 8 legal players by value, so the bot model gives those picks probability ~0. The ADP half alone scores worse than a constant base rate. The code comment at plan.js:13, 'Human GMs follow consensus ranks more than our forecasts', is contradicted by the data: real picks are explained better by the app's value than by ESPN ADP.
evidence: Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Nba-draft-simulator/bb5a3e80-4ef5-52c7-bdfc-4c0abaeb739b/scratchpad/audit/draft-plan-rookies (t4.mjs, a4.py, t5.mjs, a5b.py, a5c.py, a6b.py, t11.mjs, a7.py). Evaluation set: at each of our turns, the top 40 remaining by value, plus the top 40 by ADP, plus every player actually taken. That gives n=448 player-turns and 63 losses to opponents. App survival: Brier 0.1156, log loss 0.401. Constant base rate: Brier 0.1208. Bot half: Brier 0.1145. ADP half: Brier 0.1563. Calibration buckets (predicted -> observed): [0.99,1.0]: 1.000 -> 0.954 (n=196); [0.9,0.99): 0.958 -> 0.892; [0.8,0.9): 0.852 -> 0.738; [0,0.2): 0.15 -> 0.46. Among player-turns with app survival >=0.8 (the plan's threshold), 32 of 349 (9.2%) were taken; the model's own mean predicted loss was 3.1%. The ADP half gave survival 0.96-1.00 to every rookie actually taken in rounds 4-6 (Boozer, Wilson, Dybantsa, Lendeborg, Peterson). Spearman rank correlation of real pick number with each ranking: ADP 0.726, value 0.718; for veterans only, ADP 0.746 vs value 0.778. Conditional-logit fit on the 80 real picks over the legal sets (2-fold CV log-likelihood per pick): uniform -5.50; app's ADP model (c=1) -4.66; log-ADP only -3.62; value only -3.34; value/100 + log ADP -3.25; value/100*0.78 + 0.88*(-log ADP) + 5.19*rookie*teamNeedsRookie - 2.56*rookie*teamHasRookie -3.00. I refitted this logit leaving out each round and simulated 400 x 7 opponent picks per turn with legality checked by rejection sampling. Result: Brier 0.1060 (-8.3% vs app), log loss 0.356 (-11%), top bucket 0.994 -> 0.979.
impact: This affects every survival number the planner shows ('Шанс дожить', 'доживёт до #N') and which players get a pick deadline in the MILP. Players treated as safe were taken about 3 times more often than predicted. The draft is over, so today this only affects training mode and next season's draft. Caveat: there is only one real draft, with 63 correlated loss events.
fix: Replace the 50/50 bot/ADP mixture with a conditional logit (Plackett-Luce style) pick model: utility = b1*value/100 + b2*(-log ADP) + b3*rookie*needsRookie + b4*rookie*hasRookie. Fit it by maximum likelihood on src/fbl-draft-2026.js over the legal sets (pickCompletion), and sample opponents by softmax with rejection of illegal picks. During a live draft, update b by Bayes from the picks already recorded. Add a regression test that recomputes leave-round-out Brier and log loss on the 18.10 draft and fails if Brier exceeds the constant base rate. Today availabilityProfile and planAdvice have no tests at all.

title: adpDraft noise model: ESPN placeholder ADPs (130-141) plus noise that grows with ADP make ADP futures draft rookies around pick 75 and pick near-random late players
claim: For players ESPN users rarely draft, the ADP feed holds near-constant placeholder values: 330 of the 451 priced players with ADP sit in 130-141.4. adpDraft treats these values as real ranks and adds fresh Gaussian noise at every pick with sd = 1.5+0.2*ADP, about 29.5 for this cluster. Two consequences: (a) every rookie except Boozer, Wilson and Dybantsa sits in the 104-141 range, so ADP futures take rookies very late; (b) once real ADP candidates run out, the order inside the placeholder cluster is pure noise, not value. Because the noise scale grows with ADP, raising the noise makes the widest (worst) players win the minimum. So the model cannot be calibrated by simply widening the noise.
evidence: t6.mjs, 12 ADP drafts from the empty real state: rookies taken at picks 42-80, median about 75 (36 of 99 rookie picks at 76-80). Real draft: 32, 35, 36, 38, 42, 65, 77, 79. Bot drafts: 25-79. Thurstone likelihood of the 80 real picks under adpDraft's model with sd = c*(1.5+0.2*ADP) (a5b.py, numerical integration): c=1 (as coded) -4.66 per pick, with 20 real picks given p<1e-3; c=1.25 -3.90; c=1.5 -3.85 (best); c=2 -5.38; c=2.5 -7.92; c=4 -14.99, worse than uniform (-5.50).
impact: The ADP half of availabilityProfile says rookies and late-round players almost surely survive, which inflates the planner's rookie survival (app predicted 0.53-0.98 for rookies actually taken in rounds 4-6). This is limited now that the draft is over.
fix: Treat ADP above about 125 as censored or uninformative: rank those players by value, or use a single 'undrafted' level and break ties by value. Put the noise on a log-ADP scale with constant sd, or use the fitted logit from the previous finding. If the Thurstone form is kept, fit c by maximum likelihood (about 1.4 here).

title: Failed ADP futures are silently dropped (about 10% at pick 56), and the UI still says '50 симуляций'
claim: adpDraft checks only pickCompletion for the team on the clock. Unlike botPick (simulation.js:57), it has no cross-team rookie reservation. When rookies run short it throws 'ADP-модель не нашла допустимый пик'. availabilityProfile catches the error and skips the run (catch{continue;}). The surviving futures are therefore biased toward cases where rookies were plentiful. planAdvice also returns the requested runs count (profile:{picks,runs}) rather than the number of completed simulations, so the UI text still claims 50 simulations.
evidence: t9.mjs, real draft states, 20 seeds each: k=0, 24, 40, 48, 64, 72: 0/20 failures; k=56 (start of round 8): 2/20 ADP failures, 0/20 bot failures. availabilityProfile only reports runs:done; planAdvice line 111/121 drops it.
impact: Late-round survival estimates, exactly when rookie scarcity matters most, are conditioned on non-scarce futures, and the run count shown is overstated. The effect is small.
fix: Add the botPick reservation to adpDraft: when rookies <= teams still needing one, a team without a rookie must take one, and teams with one must skip rookies. Alternatively use the distinct-rookie matching from rookie-timing.js:52-70. Report profile.runs (done) and the number of failures in the UI.

title: Plan UI claims list FP are 'slightly lower than on the card', but they are higher for 85% of players; the method text also says opponents are only app bots
claim: The plan list and the plan chip use planValue = riskAdjustedValue*82, i.e. slotSeason (own points plus a replacement's points during long absences) minus 14% of the downside width. The player's KPI 'За сезон' shows forecast.meanSeason. The note '*ФО в списке — прогноз сезона с поправкой на риск, поэтому немного ниже, чем в карточке' is therefore false for most players. title: Rookies are valued about 140 FP/season below an equal-mean veteran in every draft ranking: no replacement credit plus a doubled downside penalty
location: scripts/projection_model.py:590-592, scripts/projection_model.py:646-658, src/valuation.js:20-24, src/valuation.js:32-36, src/plan.js:66, src/simulation.js:37-38,148
claim: draftValue uses slotSeason, which falls back to meanSeason. slotSeason/transfer are missing for all 38 priced rookies, because the replacement credit is deliberately skipped for players without an NBA record. Veterans with the same projected games get it. riskAdjustedValue then subtracts 14% of (mean - floor). Rookie ranges are much wider (relative width median 78% vs 44%), so top rookies pay about twice the penalty. The stated rationale ('the rookie rule keeps one on every roster, so he is not simply swapped out') holds only for a team's single mandatory rookie. Even then the right replacement is a rookie-level substitute, not zero. A second rookie can be swapped freely.
evidence: Priced players without slotSeason: 39 (38 rookies plus Mario Hezonja). Veterans with 66-76 projected games (n=188): transfer.value quantiles 10/25/50/75/90% = 63/73/91/109/121 FP; rookies have 70-73 games and 0. Downside penalty: Dybantsa 103, Boozer 99, Wilson 95 FP vs median 51 for veterans with mean 600-1100. planValue ranks among priced players, without vs with the median replacement credit: Dybantsa 138->108, Boozer 149->125, Wilson 165->135, Peterson 197->152, Morez Johnson 307->240. scenarioSeasonScore (simulation.js:148) likewise adds transfer.value only to veterans. Each real FBL team has exactly one rookie, so the post-draft standings effect is small.
impact: The planner objective, the bots' rankings (and so survival estimates), rookie-watch ordering and the rookie-versus-veteran draft decisions were tilted against rookies by about 1.7 FP per game played for top rookies. Draft-time only, now historical.
fix: Give rookies a replacement credit at a rookie replacement level: the best undrafted rookie per position times expected long-absence games for the mandatory rookie, and the veteran level for any extra rookie. Apply the downside allowance consistently, or drop it (see the expected-value finding). Measure it by backtesting rookie slot value on the 2024/2025 classes the way the veteran slotSeason was validated.

title: The plan's headline value is a best case, not an expectation: the full 10-pick plan is executable in only 36-54% of the app's own simulated futures
claim: planRoster maximises a deterministic sum of slot values subject to a hard per-player marginal threshold (survival >= 0.8 at the assigned pick). Players at 0.79 are excluded; players at 0.81 count fully. The chip 'N ФО' and the list read as the outcome, yet the joint probability that all planned players are still there is low. Positive correlation between players' fates is ignored, and the true marginals are worse (see the calibration finding). The optimum is very flat, so the displayed later picks are dominated by Monte Carlo noise. The risk-averse 14% downside allowance also conflicts with the league goal: to maximise P(1st of 8), a non-favourite should prefer variance, not penalise it.
evidence: t10.mjs, the app's own 50 futures: k=0 per-player survivals 1, .86, .80, .92, .88, .90, .86, .96, .82, .90; product 0.30; empirical joint probability 0.36. k=8: 0.44. k=24: 0.54. t13.mjs: at k=16, 5 of the 8 planned players differ between runs=50 and runs=100, while the plan value differs by only 0.2% (10332 vs 10311); the k=0 plan differs in 2 of 10. Threshold sensitivity at k=0: value 14334 at 0.8 vs 14999 at 0.5 (MILP, t8.mjs). Monte Carlo SE of a survival of 0.8 with 50 runs is 0.057.
impact: Users may read the plan list and its value as a forecast of the roster they will get. Only the 'now' pick is reasonably stable. Draft is over, so the impact is limited.
fix: Use a scenario-based (sample-average) stochastic MILP. For each simulated future s, add variables x_{i,r,s} with 'available in s' constraints and a shared first-stage pick, and maximise the mean over futures. This is the same constraint set times about 50 scenarios, still small for the solver (12-115 ms per solve today). Or at least maximise sum v_i*S_i(r). Show the plan's joint feasibility probability and mark later picks as indicative. Evaluate by simulating the receding-horizon policy against the calibrated opponent model and comparing mean final roster value and P(1st) via seasonSensitivitySimulations.

title: After the draft, the 'Реальный драфт' mode is not seeded from the official DRAFT_PICKS, so devices without recorded picks show a live plan for a finished draft

title: Rookie slot warnings check positions only; they miss club-limit and budget conflicts and stop once the top-5 rookies are taken
claim: rookieSlotWarnings warns 'после выбора X не останется места для rookie Y' only when !rosterFits([...roster,candidate,rookie]). It ignores the two-per-club rule and the cap, which also make the rookie illegal. It only considers the top 5 rookies overall, including ones already TAKEN, so once those 5 are gone no warning ever fires. It also warns when the team already has its rookie.
evidence: t12.mjs (real DB): team 0 takes Zach Edey (Memphis); after 7 filler picks, rookieWatch lists Boozer as AVAILABLE and rookieSlotWarnings(state, Ty Jerome [Memphis]) returns []. impact: An advisory warning is missing in club or budget cases during the draft. Hard legality is still enforced elsewhere. Draft is over.
fix: Use pickCompletion on the state after the candidate's pick for each watched rookie (positions, clubs and budget together). Watch the top 5 available rookies, not the top 5 overall. Skip the warning when the roster already has a rookie.

title: Rookie-timing statistics: the 'best round' rests on a skewed mean with weak paired evidence, and the sensitivity check is a comonotone extreme that always reports 'unstable'
claim: The recommended round is the argmax of the equal-weight mean over 4 profiles x 24 paired seeds. The reported meanGap has no uncertainty attached, and the paired comparisons show the sign is close to a coin flip. The forecastSensitivity scenario puts every rookie at P90 and every veteran at P10 at the same time, with rookie P90s at about 2.1x the mean (Dybantsa ceiling 2211 vs mean 1052). That near-impossible joint extreme flips the advice almost by construction, so the decision collapses to 'Результат неустойчив'.
evidence: t7.mjs on the fresh real DB (101 s): recommended round 4, meanGap 52.1 over round 5. Paired diffs pooled over n=96: round4-round5 mean 52.1, SE 23.2, positive in only 53% of drafts; per profile: early 78±49, middle 52±52, late 3±49, mixed 76±34. Round4-round3: mean +152.7 (SE 29.5) but positive in only 42% of drafts (driven by a skewed tail). Sensitivity: rookieUpside deltas -709..-300 ('wait'), veteranUpside -229..+644 ('unstable'), so the decision is 'unstable'.
impact: None for users today, since the module is not in the UI. If it is re-enabled, it would present a round choice with a precision it does not have.
fix: Report the paired mean ± t-interval and the share of drafts won for best vs runner-up; require the interval to exclude 0, or use a sign or Wilcoxon test with enough seeds (n≈100 per profile for a 50-FP effect at SD≈250). Replace comonotone P10/P90 with draws from each player's forecast distribution (as scenarioSeasonScore already does), and re-check the rookie P90 width with the forecast owners.

title: ESPN projection parser throws away the whole ESPN projection when ESPN leaves out a stat whose value is 0 (3PM, blocks). 24 players lose ESPN data, 21 of them centers.
claim: individual_projection() returns None whenever any of 12 stat keys is missing (`not finite(stats.get(key))`). ESPN does not send a stat that is projected as 0, so non-shooting centers have no key '17' (threesMade) and two wings have no '1' (blocks). The rejected projection leaves those players without ESPN_INDIVIDUAL. projection_model.apply then sets espn=None, so their per-game value is the career model alone and their games come from the model chain, not ESPN. This breaks the owner's rule 'Games are ESPN's alone' for exactly these players. They are also systematically undervalued against the 313 ESPN-covered players.
evidence: Deployed DB (12:41Z): 24 market players have espnContext.projectedGames but individualProjection=null. Positions: C 21, SF 1, SG 1, PG 1. A live ESPN kona_player_info GET for all 24 shows the key is missing for every one (threesMade 22, blocks 2), and the points identity 2*FGM+3PM+FTM holds with 3PM=0 for all. I rebuilt the combined forecast exactly as the code does: Jokic gives 35.00 vs 34.93 in the DB, so the method checks out. Season impact of the fix: Lively +503, Zubac 1086->1432 (+346, per game 19.67->20.75), Allen 1170->1503 (+333, 19.42->21.18), Poeltl +271, M.Robinson +249 (13.01->15.47/g), Gafford +226, Gobert 1147->1365 (+218), Hartenstein +211, Duren +148. Mark Williams goes the other way, 925->432 (ESPN 24 games, injured). Advice in the live season context: T4 'Ivica Zubac->Nikola Vucevic +184', 'Rudy Gobert->Nikola Vucevic +82' and T5 'Jarrett Allen->Nikola Vucevic +57' all disappear from bestTransfers(sort=season) once only the games part of the fix is applied.
impact: Wrong season and per-game forecasts for 24 players, among them 5 drafted starters (Zubac, Gobert, Allen, Duren, Hartenstein): per-game errors up to 2.5 FP/g, season errors from -493 to +503 FP. The Transfers tab currently shows 'sell your center' recommendations caused by this bug, and it biases every comparison at the C position.
fix: In individual_projection, require only the keys needed for identity and scale (0,13,14,15,16,40 and GP 42) and treat a missing 1/2/3/6/11/17 as 0. Keep the existing points identity check, which already guards 3PM=0. Add a unit test with a center record that has no '17'. Rebuild, then confirm 0 players have projectedGames without individualProjection.

title: CAREER_MODEL forecasts ignore ESPN return dates and out-for-season status, so the published games, season totals and '80%' ranges are impossible for long-term injured players
claim: For players without an ESPN projection, games come from the absence chain started in a generic 'not healthy' state. ESPN's returnDate and its OFS status are never used. The forecast, the season floor and ceiling, and the healthLine text ('С вероятностью 80% сыграет a–b матчей', 'в 8 сезонах из 10 результат между ними') therefore promise games after a known season-ending injury. ESPN-sourced players are not checked against the return date either.
evidence: Live ESPN injuries vs deployed DB: 11 players have forecast games above the club games scheduled after their returnDate. Ben Simmons is OFS (out until 2027-10-01) with 28.1 games, 294 FP and a claimed 80% range of 0-71 games, ceiling 634. Ariel Hukporti is out until 2027-10-01 with 49.0 games (range 18-74). Jamir Watkins is out until 2027-04-02 (6 games possible) with 50.1. Jordan Miller is out until 2027-03-02 (22 possible) with 50.6. Mark Williams (1600) is out until 2027-02-03 (33 possible) with 53.4 games / 925 FP. Rookies Oweh and Veesaar are OFS with 36.1 and 33.2 games. ESPN-sourced: Furphy 61 (48 possible), Sharpe 27 (21), Gueye 70 (65), Strawther 66 (63).
impact: Player cards in both tabs show season totals and calibrated-looking 80% claims that cannot happen, and the draft and roster ranking sorts by them. The error is up to ~500 FP for Mark Williams and up to 100% of the season for OFS players.
fix: In apply(), read the ESPN injuries endpoint (as collect_sports_current does). For OFS, or a returnDate after the season end, set games=0. Otherwise start the chain at the remaining spell length (p0 = club games before returnDate) and cap games at the club games after the return. Recompute the quantiles, then assert that games <= games possible after the return for every injured player.

title: The season tab counts injury absences twice. It also clamps the play share to at least 0.5, which inflates low-games players.
claim: playRate takes the share from forecast.games/82, clamped to [0.5, 0.97]. For an injured player whose forecast games already exclude the absence (ESPN games), expectedPoints zeroes every game before returnDate and then applies that already-reduced share again to the games after the return. The 0.5 floor maps any forecast under 41 games (rotation risk, injury-shortened ESPN projections, undrafted rookies) to about 40 games. The in-season calibration fitted only the prior weight, with the previous season's raw games as prior and no injury report ('no injury report is used in the backtest'). This combination was never validated.
evidence: Live context, season horizon: Jimmy Butler (ESPN 39 g, out until 2027-01-02, 48 club games after) gets 25.4 games / 526 FP vs 39 / 808. Porzingis 44.0 vs 59 (725 vs 973), Ingram 48.7 vs 55, Claxton 61.6 vs 69, Strus 59.1 vs 67, Nurkic 57.3 vs 64. A fix that expresses forecast games as a share of the games after the return gives Butler 39.8 / 825 and Porzingis 58.3 / 961. The floor inflates others: Moses Moody 12 -> 31 games (341 vs 132 FP, 2.6x), Topic 25.9 -> 39.7, Sorber 17.1 -> 39.5, Alpha Diallo and other undrafted rookies 17.1 -> 40 (207 vs 88 FP), and 47 healthy market players under 41 forecast games are all set to ~40. Backtest check (my run of inseason_calibration cases): the floor helps only for a raw previous-season prior (MAE 0.1896 vs 0.1928 unclamped).
impact: Injured players who will play are undervalued by 13-37% in transfer options, injured targets, team 'forecast per period' and explainSwap. Low-games players and undrafted rookies are overvalued by 1.5-2.6x, which matters when the rookie rule forces a rookie swap.
fix: Compute the share from a baseline that excludes the injury, e.g. availability.unconditionalGames or sources.model.games over 82, or for an injured player forecast.games / club games after returnDate. Apply the [.5,.97] clamp only to a raw previous-season prior. Refit and validate with an injury-aware backtest once 2026/27 checkpoints exist.

title: ESPN games (313 players) are used next to model games (500 players). ESPN is +8.9 games above the model for the same healthy players, while the model's healthy-start holdout bias is -0.66 games.
claim: The code says 'the absence chain predicts too few games for players who start healthy'. The published holdout says otherwise: healthyStartBias -0.656 (MAE 13.36, n=296). The large bias is only in the unconditional variant (-4.2). For the same 265 healthy ESPN-covered players, ESPN projects 8.98 more games than the healthy-start model (+15.6 games in the 40-55 model-games bucket). If 2025/26 is representative, ESPN games are optimistic by about 8 games. The 313 ESPN players are inflated about 12% against the CAREER_MODEL players (all 24 centers of finding 1, plus 119 market players with no ESPN projection), and every cross-source comparison carries this bias.
evidence: Deployed DB, ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED: mean(espn.games - model.games) = 8.92 (median 8.19, n=313; healthy only 8.98, n=265). By model-games bucket: 40-55 -> +15.6 (n=61), 55-65 -> +6.7 (n=131), 65-75 -> +5.6 (n=64). projection-model-audit holdout.healthyStart: unconditionalBias -4.235, healthyStartBias -0.656.
impact: The bias is systematic, about +9 games (~12% season FP) for ESPN-covered players compared with model-only players. It feeds playRate priors, season gains and the draft ranking. The ESPN bias itself is inferred, not measured, because no ESPN projection archive exists.
fix: Use one games source for everyone, or shrink ESPN toward the model: games = model + w*(ESPN - model), with w=0 until it is validated. Archive ESPN's 2026/27 pre-season games now (snapshot the feed) so that paired MAE and bias of ESPN games vs model games can be measured on 2026/27, and refit w then.

title: sportsCheck flags and the 'Рост/Спад на Sports.ru' insights compare a forecast without the bonus to Sports.ru history that includes the ±2.5 team-result bonus
claim: Since 20.10 the forecast has no team-result bonus. Sports.ru's printed per-game history still contains it, so the gap compares numbers on different scales. The +/-15% flag ('Прогноз расходится с прошлым сезоном Sports.ru на X%: проверь роль и здоровье') and the season-to-season trend are partly about team wins, not the player. insights is shared with the Telegram verdicts. Only the main.js history table carries a disclaimer.
evidence: 390 players with sportsCheck season 2025-26 and 20+ parquet games: Sports.ru per game minus our FBL (no-bonus) per game from game_logs_2025-26 has mean 0.035, sd 0.847, range -1.95..+1.86. OLS of that difference on team win% gives a=-2.49 and b=4.99, which is exactly a ±2.5 per-game bonus. On the same basis, 76 of 390 flags flip (114 flagged now vs 90). Examples: Chris Youngblood (OKC .85) gap -1% vs +64% without bonus, Jaden Hardy (.23) +47% vs +9%, Kevon Looney +37% vs +7%. The forecasts themselves do not depend on the bonus: regressing forecast minus last-season FBL on win% gives slope 0.03 (CAREER_MODEL) and -0.02 (combined).
impact: About 20% of the 'forecast disagrees with Sports.ru' warnings are wrong in either direction, and trend pros and cons move by up to ±2 FP/g with team record changes. These texts appear in player cards and the Telegram verdicts.
fix: Subtract the bonus from each Sports.ru season (team W/L per game is in the logs or the calendar), or compare with our own FBL per game from the parquet logs. Label the Sports.ru numbers 'с бонусом' wherever insights quote them.

title: Displayed absence-spell rates are scaled hazards, not 'по логам'. DiVincenzo shows 174 short spells per 82 games (hazard 2.12 per game > 1).
claim: availability.hazards and shortSpellsPer82/longSpellsPer82 are the personal hazards multiplied by the scale c, which forces the chain mean onto the regression or ESPN games. When ESPN's games encode a known long injury (DiVincenzo, Achilles, ESPN 4 games) and the chain starts 'healthy', c explodes. The UI then prints these numbers as 'Здоровье по логам 2002–2026 … коротких пропусков N за 82 матча при M у ровесников', which is neither from the logs nor physically possible. The Python chain caps each hazard at 0.45 per frailty point, but the published values and the JS chainCurve use them uncapped.
evidence: Deployed DB: Donte DiVincenzo hazards [2.122, 0.486] per game, shortSpellsPer82 174.0 and longSpellsPer82 39.9, vs league 6.85/1.74, gamesRange [0,11]. 35 market players show more than 20 short spells per 82 (Alex Morales 62.6, Zyon Pullin 45.0, Riley Minix 37.7). Median personal/league ratio on the market is 0.57.
impact: The UI states false health statistics in the draft and season player cards. The 'health' story for fringe players is really DNP-coach's-decision risk relabelled as injuries.
fix: Store and display the unscaled personal rates (ns/e and nl/e from hazards()), and keep the scaled ones only for the chain. Clip display to at most 82 per 82. For known long injuries, start the chain in the absence state (see the injury-start finding) instead of inflating c. Change the label to 'с учётом прогноза числа матчей' if scaled rates are shown.

title: 2025 draftees who never played (Sorber #15, Markovic #47) are labelled and forecast as undrafted rookies
claim: apply() looks for a draft pick only in DRAFT_YEAR==TARGET-1 (2026) or in drafts['2026'] by name. A 2025 pick with no NBA games falls back to the UNDRAFTED_ROOKIE_MODEL prior, and the UI basis says 'Модель незадрафтованных новичков'.
evidence: data/nba-drafts.json 2025: Thomas Sorber overall 15, Bogoljub Markovic overall 47. Deployed DB: both are origin UNDRAFTED_ROOKIE_MODEL, draftPick null, 5.16 FP/g x 17.1 games = 88 FP. The 2026 #12 pick Aday Mara has 8.25 x 51.4 = 424. Season tab: Sorber 39.5 games after the 0.5 floor.
impact: Two isRookie players (both count toward the rookie rule) get a wrong label and a likely understated pick-based prior (Sorber, 1100). The label shown to users is false.
fix: Look up the pick in every draft year up to TARGET-1 for players without NBA games (and possibly add a 'deferred debut' covariate). Add a test that every name in drafts['2025'] without games gets DRAFT_PICK_MODEL.

title: The healthy-start flag reads injuries from the ESPN roster endpoint. It misses Johnny Furphy's long injury and treats day-to-day players as unhealthy.
claim: player.injuries comes from athlete.injuries in teams/{id}/roster. That source omits some injuries listed by the injuries endpoint used by the season tab, and it gives the same weight to Day-To-Day and Out. healthy=not injuries therefore gives healthyNow=True to an injured player and denies the validated healthy-start uplift to minor GTD cases.
evidence: Live espnInjuries has 90 injured players. 89 match the DB injuries; Johnny Furphy (Out, return 2027-01-02, reported 2026-02-09) has DB injuries=[], healthyNow=True and 61 games (48 possible). The 15 CAREER_MODEL market players listed only as GTD (e.g. Moussa Diabate, Oso Ighodaro, Pelle Larsson) have games = unconditionalGames. The mean healthy uplift for healthy CAREER_MODEL players is +2.8 games (n=115).
impact: Small. Furphy +13 games (~90 FP). 15 fringe players are about 3 games low.

title: ESPN ADP is censored at about 130-141 for 75% of players but is used as a rank in 'Недооценён рынком' insights and in draft-opponent simulation

title: Games on the transfer date count for the wrong FBL team: buyers get the night's points the player scored before he was bought
claim: stints() opens the buyer's stint and closes the seller's on the journal date x.date. teamPoints/teamFact/playerFact then count a game when g.date>=s.from && g.date<s.to. Sports.ru files every game under the Moscow date of its tip-off (src/live.js moscowDate: 'the date Sports.ru files that game under'). A normal US-evening game therefore carries the Moscow date D and ends by about 07:30 MSK on D, while FBL transfers are allowed only 08:00-22:00 MSK. So every night game dated D was already over when a transfer on D happened. The code credits the incoming player's finished game to the buyer and drops the outgoing player's game from the seller's own total. Sports.ru says transfers take effect immediately and players are locked during their games. Yahoo's 'Daily - Today' setting applies a change to the current US day. Neither platform gives a buyer a game that is already over. The existing test avoids the edge case, because neither player in it has a game on the transfer date.
evidence: Reproduction (node scratchpad/audit/scoring-rules-grey/stint.mjs): team 0 holds player 1 (40 FP in a game dated 2026-10-22) and buys player 81 (55 FP in a game dated 2026-10-22) on 2026-10-22. teamPoints returns 55; the correct value is 40. Date convention checked on a real Sports.ru 2025/26 page: Phoenix's play-in game against Portland on 14.04.2026 (US date) is filed as '15.04.2026' (ESPN career log, UTC: 2026-04-15, PHX-POR, L 110-114). The live calendar's weekday counts (Thu 452 busiest, Fri 272 lightest) also fit Moscow dates of US Wed/Thu games. Magnitude from a simulation on 2025/26 logs of the 69 drafted FBL players with logs (scratchpad/audit/scoring-rules-grey/stint_mag.py): 57% of random transfers fall on a date on which the bought or the sold player has a game. Mean absolute error 10.0 FP per transfer, SD 15.4. SD of the error in a team's season total: 98 FP over 40 transfers, 120 FP over 60. A manager who buys the best of 5 candidates by last night's game gains +13.4 FP of credit per transfer. Adjacent-team gap in the 2025/26 replay of the drafted rosters: 253 FP.
impact: Wrong 'official' team totals, weekly and period facts, player facts and 'Место в лиге' on the Overview and Teams tabs. The error is biased in favour of managers who chase hot players. A weekly table can be off by 10-40 FP per transfer.
fix: Assign each game by its tip-off time, not its date. Store the ESPN event start time (already fetched in live.js), or treat games dated D as played before any transfer on D unless they start after 08:00 MSK. A minimal fix that is right for about 95% of games: count a game for the buyer when g.date > s.from and for the seller when g.date <= s.to. Where seenAt is known, compare it with the game start time instead. Add a test with a game on the transfer date for both players.

title: Grey zone for the league owner: Yahoo category totals cannot reproduce the +2/+1 by 10 minutes term, but the app scores with the exact minutes rule
location: data/league-rules.json:119-155 (yahoo block, never read by code), scripts/collect_sports_current.py:206-232, scripts/projection_model.py:197-206, src/season.js:420-427, docs/ACCEPTANCE.md:227
claim: Per data/league-rules.json, the league totals Yahoo categories (GP, FGA, FGM, FTA, FTM, PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK, TO, PF) with the FBL formula. Yahoo has no minutes category, so the participation term can only be k*GP. It cannot be +2 for 10+ minutes and +1 below. The app scores all forecasts, live game points and team totals with the exact minutes rule: Sports.ru ФО minus the result bonus, model rate = pm*minutes + 2 - short. No code reads the recorded Yahoo settings. docs/ACCEPTANCE.md:227 says Yahoo has 'the same categories as Sports.ru's formula'. That is false: the formula needs minutes, and GP is not one of its terms. Which constant the league applies per GP is not documented anywhere.
evidence: From the 2025/26 logs (exact MM:SS minutes; scratchpad/audit/scoring-rules-grey/participation.py): 4,017 of 26,648 player-games (15.1%) were under 10 minutes. Players with 20+ games: 17.4% of their games; 60 players had at least half their games under 10 minutes. Rotation players (20+ mpg): 2.5%. Per player-season with 20+ GP, '2 per GP' exceeds the exact rule by 7.7 FP on average, up to 41. '1 per GP' falls 48.7 FP short. Replaying the 8 drafted FBL rosters on 2025/26 (teams_participation.py): 1-7 short games per team-season, so 2*GP is within 7 FP of the exact rule. 1*GP lowers team totals by the team's GP (387-631 FP per team-season, about 5%) and moves team gaps by up to 244 FP; the smallest adjacent gap is 253 FP. Pool view: 213 of the 517 forecast players on current rosters have a participation term below 1.9 and 38 below 1.5, i.e. up to 1 FP/game on cheap bench options in transfer advice. Independent check against Sports.ru's own season totals (vs_sports_espn.py, 354 clean player-seasons): the exact rule plus the bonus fits better than 2/GP (mean residual +0.29 vs -3.31 FP/season). So Sports.ru does apply the 10-minute rule; the league's Yahoo-based count cannot.
impact: All absolute numbers shown as the league's (team totals, per-game forecasts, live points) and the rankings of bench and low-minute players. With 2*GP the difference is negligible for current rosters. With 1*GP every number is off by about 1 FP per game, and team gaps shift by the difference in games played.
fix: Ask the league owner which participation constant the league applies to Yahoo GP (2, 1 or other) and whether the 10-minute split matters at all. Record it as data/league-rules.json scoringFormula.participation = 'EXACT_MINUTES' | 'PER_GP_2' | 'PER_GP_1'. Apply it in one place: collect_sports_current.fbl_points (subtract the Sports.ru participation and add the league constant), projection_model.predict (rate = pm*minutes + c), build_forecasts.full and boxScorePoints. Correct the ACCEPTANCE line 227 wording.

title: The 'independent' scoring audit (78,901 games, 0 mismatches) compares the formula with itself; an external check against Sports.ru's totals is possible and passes

The '+1 turnover = -2' check is a constant. The forecast checks are identities by construction: projection_model.stat_line defines components['adjustment'] = rate - sum(others), so the sum of components equals meanPerGame by design. An independent test exists in the repo's own data: Sports.ru's official season totals (data/sports-fantasy-history.json) against ESPN logs with result and home.

impact: A false sense of verification. The formula and bonus are in fact right (see the reconciliation), but the published audit would not have caught an error.

title: ESPN minutes are rounded, so live box-score points give +2 to 9:30-9:59 appearances where Sports.ru gives +1
